suggestion.title: Clipboard Monitor + Wallet Address Replacement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'clipboard theft, wallet replacement' as core capability; no use case targets clipboard API monitoring or unexpected modifications to clipboard contents before paste events. Article phrase: 'combines clipboard theft, wallet replacement'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes accessing clipboard APIs (ClipboardData, GetClipboardOwner, OpenClipboard) in unusual contexts (non-browser, non-editor), especially correlating with writes to wallet-adjacent registry keys or local file modifications. Flag when clipboard contents deviate from user's source application immediately before a transaction.

suggestion.title: Tor Client Instantiation by Non-Network Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Tor-based communications' for C2; describes it as core persistence and control mechanism. No use case covers unexpected Tor process spawning or network redirection to Tor nodes from suspicious processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Tor browser/tor.exe process creation by processes not in a whitelist (legitimate Tor Browser installer, user-initiated), especially from %AppData%, %Temp%, or download directories. Correlate with unusual network destinations or SOCKS5 proxy configuration in child processes.

suggestion.title: Worm-Like Propagation via File/Network Share Enumeration + Self-Copy
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'worm-like propagation for persistence'; indicates lateral movement mechanism. No use case covers the enumeration and replication pattern. Article phrase: 'worm-like propagation'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid enumeration of network shares (\\\\*\\c$, IPC$), discovery of user home directories, or recursive file-system traversal followed by copy operations to those destinations. Flag when a single process spawns multiple copies of itself across network paths in short time window.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Callback to Tor Hidden Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'establishes persistent access and enables follow-on activity through a lightweight backdoor capability' — this implies scheduled or triggered beaconing to a Tor endpoint. No use case covers backdoor callback signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry/scheduled-task creation (Run, RunOnce, Task Scheduler) pointing to unsigned or freshly-created executables in temp/appdata; correlate spawning Tor client or SOCKS proxy communication within 30 seconds. Flag if process communicates outbound to .onion domains or Tor entry node IPs.

suggestion.title: Crypto Wallet Application Data Exfiltration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Clipper malware targets cryptocurrency wallets; article describes stealing transactions and establishing persistent access. No use case covers suspicious file access to wallet storage paths (MetaMask, Exodus, etc.) or unusual read-copy patterns to exfil staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access to wallet-store paths (%AppData%\\MetaMask, Exodus, etc.) by non-wallet executables; flag when wallet config/seed files are read and subsequently copied to staging or piped to network sockets. Correlate with Tor process spawning.

suggestion.title: Unsigned/Recently-Created Binary Execution from Non-Standard Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'persistent access' and 'backdoor capability' implying file-based persistence; worm propagation implies dropped files. No use case covers execution of unsigned malware dropped to temp/cache/startup folders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned, recently-created (.CreationTime < 24h), low-reputation binaries executed from %Temp%, %ProgramData%, Downloads, or Startup folders; especially if process then spawns network or clipboard-monitoring children.

suggestion.title: XXE Proof-of-Concept Payload in Request Body — HAPI FHIR Saxon Transform
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is triggered via `saxonTransform()` receiving untrusted XSLT input: 'unhardened Saxon TransformerFactory' instantiation. Detection should hunt for HTTP requests with XML containing DOCTYPE declarations or external entity syntax targeting FHIR endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT to FHIR endpoints (*/fhir/*, */hl7/fhir/*) with payloads containing <!DOCTYPE or <!ENTITY declarations, or XML with SYSTEM protocol scheme. Inspect request body for XML External Entity signatures.

suggestion.title: Local File Access via XXE — File Disclosure Attempts
suggestion.rationale: XXE vulnerabilities are exploited for local file disclosure. Article describes 'unprotected' TransformerFactory allowing ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD and ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET. Detection should identify attempts to resolve file:// URIs or reading of /etc/passwd, /etc/hosts, or configuration files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed DTD resolution events in application logs with corresponding file-access attempts from the Java process. Look for error messages containing 'file://', 'DOCTYPE', or 'entity not allowed' paired with Filesystem events for sensitive paths.

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band XML External Entity Callback Server Detection
suggestion.rationale: XXE is often exploited via OOB exfiltration using attacker-controlled callback domain. Article mentions 'OOB exfil' explicitly in UC_5_3. Detection should identify Java processes connecting to rare/new external hosts with XML-shaped URIs in DNS queries or HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DNS requests from Java/FHIR processes to uncommon external domains immediately following an HTTP request to a FHIR endpoint. Look for callback hostnames matching OOB exfil patterns (e.g., attacker.com/callback?data=...).

suggestion.title: XSLT Transform Error Spikes from Malformed XML Input
suggestion.rationale: XXE exploitation attempts will trigger XML parsing and XSLT validation errors. Article specifies the vulnerability is in XSLT transform processing ('XsltUtilities.saxonTransform'). Detection should hunt for error rate anomalies in Saxon transformer logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline error rates for XML parsing and XSLT transformation in FHIR application logs. Alert when error count from a single source exceeds 3-sigma baseline within 5-minute window, filtering for 'DOCTYPE', 'ENTITY', 'permission denied', 'access denied' keywords.

suggestion.title: High-volume bytes-per-source to /api/v1/upload endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Unauthenticated users can upload any amount of data to the server without any limitations' and 'This can lead to space exhaustion on the server.' Existing UC_6_3 detects upload count spike, but not absolute data volume per single source (attacker could do slow upload still exhausting disk).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate HTTP bytes_in by source IP to /api/v1/upload/* endpoint over 1-hour windows. Alert if single source exceeds 5–10GB threshold (tuned to Langflow hardware). Combine with UC_6_4 filesystem growth to confirm disk exhaustion attack (not legitimate batch model upload).

suggestion.title: Execution or network anomaly following large Langflow upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1204.002 (User Execution: Malicious File) as attack technique, implying uploaded content may be executed. Current UCs focus on DoS and disclosure; none detect file execution post-upload. If attacker uploads executable and Langflow processes it, should detect child-process spawning (shells, interpreters, curl, wget).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting large upload to /api/v1/upload (UC_6_3 or UC_6_6 trigger), monitor Langflow/Python parent process for child spawning of shells (bash, cmd.exe), interpreters (python, perl), or network tools (curl, wget) within 30 seconds. High confidence if child process has network outbound or reads from /tmp or cache directories.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated flow_id enumeration before upload attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions '/api/v1/upload/{flow_id}' endpoint, implying attacker must know or guess flow_id. Sophisticated attacks may enumerate valid flow_ids via GET requests before attempting upload. Current UCs only detect POST; missing reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequence of GET requests to /api/v1/upload/* (or /api/v1/flows/*) from single source with mixed HTTP response codes (404 for invalid IDs, 200 for valid), without prior authentication. >50 requests in <5 minutes = enumeration pattern. Correlate with subsequent POST uploads to same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Langflow service file-descriptor or resource exhaustion indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states uploads without limits can exhaust 'space,' and DoS result is system-wide disk full. Detection should include system-level indicators (inode exhaustion, failed write operations, filesystem full events) beyond application-layer uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor filesystem for 'No space left on device' errors (syslog level), disk-full alerts from OS, or failed-write operations where path matches Langflow cache directories. Correlate with Langflow process still running. Alert if write failures occur >10 times in 5m window on cache partition.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML Tampering Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploiting XML files in Windows recovery partition (title: 'Recovery Partition XML Files'). Pipeline missed detection for malicious XML modification in EFI/recovery volumes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation, modification, or access to Windows recovery partition XML configuration files (typically in \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy or recovery environment paths). Flag XML parsing or DOM manipulation in SYSTEM context targeting BitLocker configuration.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Bypass Attempt via Recovery Volume
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome: 'bypasses Windows BitLocker.' Pipeline should detect attempts to access, mount, or modify recovery partitions that contain BitLocker unlock keys or configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes with SYSTEM privileges accessing recovery partition mountpoints, reading BitLocker metadata files, or executing PowerShell commands with BitLocker-related cmdlets (Get-BitLockerVolume, Disable-BitLocker) preceded by recovery partition activity.

suggestion.title: GreatXML Exploit Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Named exploit 'GreatXML' in title; no IOC extraction occurred. Pipeline should flag any process creation, file write, or command-line invocation of this named tool.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution or creation of files named GreatXML, greatxml, or variants; monitor for unexpected tool usage in recovery environment or WinPE context; alert on parent-child relationships linking user sessions to recovery-boot-stage processes.

suggestion.title: Evasion via Pre-OS Boot Persistence
suggestion.rationale: BitLocker bypass via recovery partition is a pre-OS boot attack; pipeline failed to map this to T1542 (Pre-OS Boot). Recovery partition code runs before OS security checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for attempts to persist code in EFI variables, NVRAM settings, or recovery partition boot sectors. Alert on tools that manipulate UEFI/BIOS configuration or recovery partition boot order; correlate with BitLocker configuration changes.

suggestion.title: XML Parsing Anomalies in Boot Context
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly uses 'XML Files' (title). Pipeline missed detection for XML deserialization, entity expansion (XXE), or namespace hijacking in recovery environment context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious XML parsing libraries (msxml, xml2, libxml2) or DOM operations invoked from recovery partition, WinPE, or pre-boot environment. Monitor for large or malformed XML documents in recovery volumes.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Configuration Manipulation Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: After bypassing BitLocker via recovery partition exploit, attacker would need to modify BitLocker state or unlock volumes. Pipeline missed detection for BitLocker key exfiltration or volume unlock.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows BitLocker event logs (sources 4693, 4694) for unexpected recovery key unlock or volume disable events. Alert on PowerShell BitLocker cmdlets invoked outside of IT maintenance windows. Cross-correlate with recovery partition access.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor (CVE-2026-48907)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited' and provides template guidance for asset-exposure hunt. No UC was generated despite explicit direction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed instances of Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor running unpatched versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-48907. Query asset database for product version, cross-reference against patch due date (2026-06-19). High false-negative risk; prioritize public-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla editor profile creation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Pipeline missed the profile-creation step entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla Content Editor endpoints for POST requests to profile/configuration creation endpoints from unauthenticated sessions (no active session cookie). Look for patterns like `/index.php?option=com_joomcontent&task=profile` or similar variant creation endpoints without prior auth.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP code upload via Joomla editor
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'upload and execution of PHP code' as the exploitation mechanism. No execution/upload detection UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new PHP files written to Joomla content editor directories post-profile creation, especially from web-server process context. Correlate with preceding unauthenticated profile creation requests. High specificity: filter for Joomla-managed directories only to reduce noise.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor remote code execution post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states uploaded PHP code can be 'executed'; pipeline did not map to T1059 or post-exploitation activity. Need detection for actually *running* uploaded payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution initiated by web-server user (www-data / IUSR) spawning shells, interpreters, or reverse-shell patterns immediately after PHP file creation in Joomla directories. Baseline: web server should not spawn cmd.exe, /bin/sh, or nc.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the attack surface—no existing session validation. Detection should baseline legitimate profile creation and flag unauthenticated attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla logs for successful editor profile creation events (typically logged with action='com_plugins.profile.create' or equivalent) originating from requests with no valid session tokens or from the unauthenticated guest user context. Correlate with HTTP POST to editor profile endpoints lacking valid Joomla authorization headers.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Joomla Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Attackers weaponize the access-control bypass to upload webshells. Monitor for .php uploads to editor-related directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PHP file uploads to Joomla editor profile storage directories (or immediate subdirs) in application event logs. Cross-reference with T1059 signatures on subsequent PHP process execution in those directories. High-fidelity signal if PHP appears in directories typically containing .xml config or media assets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV (actively exploited in wild) with federal remediation due 2026-06-19. Use asset-exposure hunt pattern to detect vulnerable Joomla Content Editor instances via scanner output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Joomla instances in your fleet and alert on scanner CVE matches for CVE-2026-48907. Cross-reference with patch-applied dates to identify lag. CISA KEV listings historically precede exploit activity by days—time-critical.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Joomla Editor Configuration/Profile Additions
suggestion.rationale: Article's attack vector is 'creation of new editor profiles.' Legitimate administrators provision editors via menus; attackers are creating them via direct unauthenticated access. Detect profile count/config changes outside change windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla database logs (jos_extensions, jos_plugins tables if profiles stored there) for INSERT/UPDATE events creating new editor profiles outside approved change-control windows. Correlate with requests lacking CSRF tokens or session validation in the same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Joomla Widget Factory Content Editor Plugin Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Widget Factory, Product: Joomla Content Editor' on internet-facing instances. CISA KEV designation means active exploitation in wild. Pipeline generated zero asset-inventory use case despite having CVE, vendor, product, and severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Joomla installations with Widget Factory Content Editor plugin installed. Cross-reference plugin version against CVE-2026-48907 patch threshold. Alert on any public-facing (external-IP, global DNS) Joomla instances running vulnerable versions matching federal patch-due-date 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Pipeline did not translate explicit behavioral indicator to detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to Joomla editor profile endpoints (e.g., /index.php?option=com_content&task=profile* or widget factory component routes) where source IP has no prior successful authentication. Flag if response code is 2xx (success). Correlate with subsequent file writes to /components/, /plugins/, /media/.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Joomla Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Attack conclusion is 'execution of PHP code'; article implies attacker-controlled PHP in web-accessible path. Pipeline omitted execution-phase detection entirely (kill-chain phases empty).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process spawning (apache, php-fpm, httpd child processes) from Joomla component/plugin/media directories within seconds of HTTP POST to profile endpoints. Alert on suspicious .php file writes to web-accessible Joomla paths immediately before process spawn. Baseline: legitimate plugin updates vs. unauthorized uploads.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Joomla Plugin Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'improper access control,' not just unauthenticated upload. Implies config/profile mutation by unprivileged or unauthenticated actors. Pipeline missed this persistence/configuration-tampering angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla plugin configuration tables and profile serialized objects in DB for changes originating from requests without authenticated session tokens. Alert on profile creation where user_id is null or guest role. Track editor component manifest files for unauthorized additions.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Joomla Widget Factory Content Editor Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' as vulnerable product and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using CVE-2026-48907. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Joomla installations with the vulnerable Content Editor plugin. Query asset inventory and web proxy logs for requests to /components/com_widgetfactory/ or characteristic editor paths. Establish baseline of exposed instances against patch due date (2026-06-19).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—this is the initial exploitation foothold. Pipeline missed detection for this critical step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla Content Editor profile creation endpoints for requests without valid authentication tokens or sessions. Alert on profile creation from external/untrusted IPs. Correlate with subsequent file uploads to the same session or user context.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via Content Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code via...editor profiles.' Pipeline missed the upload vector entirely despite it being the exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php/.phtml file uploads to Joomla Content Editor component directories and temp/cache paths during or after suspicious profile creation. Cross-reference upload timestamps with subsequent PHP execution in web server process logs.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution Post-Content Editor Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once PHP code is uploaded, attacker executes commands on the server. Article describes 'upload and execution' but pipeline failed to model the execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After Content Editor exploitation detected, hunt for anomalous PHP child processes (bash, curl, wget) spawned from web server processes. Monitor for POST/GET requests with command parameters to newly uploaded PHP files. Flag exec(), system(), passthru() calls in PHP logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scan Matches
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'CVE-2026-48907 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as primary IOC. Pipeline returned no IOCs despite this direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48907 matches across all assets. Prioritize externally-exposed Joomla instances. Track time-to-remediation against federal due date (2026-06-19). Escalate any matches to patch management pipeline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Go Module Import - Typo Squatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names github.com/botdb-go/bolt as malicious typo squat of github.com/boltdb/bolt: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod/go.sum file modifications and Go build process arguments for imports of similarly-named packages (github.com/botdb-go/bolt vs. boltdb/bolt, etc.). Alert on character-distance typos of known legitimate packages appearing in dependency manifests.

suggestion.title: Malicious Go Module Version 1.3.1 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific malicious version: 'The harmful version (1.3.1) was released on GitHub in November 2021.' Versions in manifests are concrete observables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse go.mod and go.sum files; alert when github.com/botdb-go/bolt@1.3.1 or version ranges containing it appear. Cross-reference against supply-chain threat feeds for known-malicious module versions.

suggestion.title: Go Module Mirror Cache Poisoning - Persistence Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes caching-based persistence: 'the Go Module Mirror service stored it permanently... Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module.' This is the mechanism enabling 3-year dwell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go toolchain requests to proxy.golang.org (Go Module Proxy) for packages with CVE/known-malicious listings. Alert on cache-hit behaviors for modules flagged in vulnerability database post-removal date, indicating persistence via stale cache.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Command and Control - Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states C2 capability: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from hosts that imported/executed github.com/botdb-go/bolt. Alert on anomalous DNS queries, suspicious IP connections, periodic beaconing patterns, or command channel communication consistent with remote backdoor control.

suggestion.title: Forced Dependency Update Triggering Malicious Module Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes update mechanism as attack vector: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Routine updates became infection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go package manager operations (go get, go mod tidy, go mod update) that pull from typo-squatted or suspicious package names. Alert when dependency updates introduce newly-cached versions of previously-removed malicious modules.

suggestion.title: Joomla CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template and CVE-2026-48907 as a CISA KEV entry 'observed exploited in the wild'; this is the primary detection for exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-48907 in Joomla Content Editor. Prioritize unpatched externally-facing instances; cross-check patch deployment dates against CISA federal due date (2026-06-19).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' followed by code upload. This is the exploitation foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to Joomla editor profile endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php) from unauthenticated sessions lacking valid auth tokens or matching baseline profile-creation patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Upload to Joomla Content Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code' as the attack outcome; detect .php/.php5 uploads to content/ and images/ directories from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php/.php5 file uploads to Joomla content, images, or plugins directories, especially from unauthenticated sources or after editor profile creation anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Joomla Editor Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execution of PHP code' through the compromised editor workflow; execution signals detection needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php.exe/php-cgi spawned from Joomla content paths or HTTP requests to newly-uploaded .php files in content directories matching the upload timestamps.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Joomla Content Editor Profile Creation (CVE-2026-48907)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—this is the entry point. Pipeline missed the unauthenticated access abnormality entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla Content Editor endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php?option=com_editors) for profile creation requests (POST) lacking valid admin session tokens or coming from IP ranges never seen creating profiles. Flag if profile creation succeeds from unauthenticated context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Upload to Joomla Web Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code'—critical execution mechanism the pipeline did not decompose into detectable file I/O.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .php file writes to web-accessible Joomla directories (components, modules, templates) immediately following a suspicious profile creation or editor access. Correlation: file write timestamp + HTTP request execution of that URI path within seconds.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should have generated direct CVE scanning use case. Article names CVE-2026-48907 and provides 10-day federal patch window (due 2026-06-19)—urgent asset-inventory correlation is a canonical first hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results or WAF signatures for CVE-2026-48907 exploitation attempts against Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor versions. Match public exploit payloads (if available) against web logs for 'profile=' or 'editor=' parameters with encoded PHP payloads.

suggestion.title: Joomla Administrator Access from Unauthenticated Context
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'improper access control' lets unauth users reach functions meant for authenticated admins. Pipeline did not surface access-control violation as a detection pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla /administrator paths for requests that lack valid session cookies or authenticate as 'Guest' user, but still receive 200-class responses (indicating access granted). Flag if such requests carry parameters typically associated with admin operations (option=com_editors, task=profile.*)

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution in Joomla Content Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies PHP execution post-upload. Pipeline failed to identify T1505.002 (Web Shell) persistence/execution technique, which is the aftermath of successful file upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to recently-created .php files in Joomla content paths (monitor file creation timestamps via file integrity monitoring or WAF logs, then correlate to subsequent HTTP GET/POST requests to those URIs). Look for PHP execution indicators (subprocess spawning, database connections from web process, outbound network connections).

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Check for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal due date 2026-06-19 and emphasis on patch-lag risk. Pipeline should have generated audit-driven compliance hunt beyond basic CVE scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor plugin/extension version. Flag all instances below patched version threshold or where installation date post-2026-06-19 without evidence of emergency patching. Cross-correlate with CVE-2026-48907 web scanner findings to prioritize remediation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Joomla Editor Profile Creation by Unauthenticated User
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the vulnerability's entry point and should be the primary detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_*editor*) from sessions lacking valid authentication tokens or auth cookies. Baseline legitimate profile-creation frequency; any spike or unauthenticated success is suspicious.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Joomla Editor Component
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Execution requires file upload first.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multipart POST uploads to editor-related endpoints with .php/.phtml extensions or MIME mismatches (application/x-php offered as image/jpeg). Correlate with editor profile creation in same session to identify exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Web Shell PHP Execution Post-Upload in Joomla Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'execution of PHP code'; once uploaded, attacker invokes it. Web shell execution is the post-exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GET/POST requests to newly created .php files in Joomla root or component directories within hours of suspicious uploads. Look for common web-shell indicators: cmd=, shell=, encoded payloads, or requests from unusual ASNs/geolocations post-upload.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CVE-2026-48907' explicitly. CISA KEV entries require immediate inventory and patch tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48907 matches against Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instances. Federal due-date is 2026-06-19; flag any unpatched installs exposed to the internet as critical risk.

suggestion.title: Access-Control Bypass HTTP Responses to Joomla Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'improper access control.' Detection should flag unexpected 200/302 responses to protected admin paths from unauthenticated clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200 or 302 responses to /administrator/* or component-specific admin paths when source session lacks valid authentication cookies or bearer tokens. Compare baseline authentication success rates per source to detect ACL bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Detect anomalous POST requests to Joomla editor profile endpoints from non-admin sources or at atypical times.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT to Joomla administrator editor profile creation endpoints (com_jce or content-editor paths) from IPs outside trusted admin subnets. Successful exploitation requires reaching this endpoint unauthenticated.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Media/Plugins Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code'—attacker must write PHP files to web-accessible directories. Detect .php creation in editor-controlled or media paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of .php or .phtml files in /media/jce*, /plugins/editors*, or /administrator/components/com_jce* directories written by web-server processes (Apache/Nginx/php-fpm). High confidence post-exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: Web-Server Process Code Execution Following Upload
suggestion.rationale: Attack culminates in 'execution of PHP code.' After file upload detected, look for abnormal process spawning, command execution, or network activity initiated from web-server context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PHP file uploads to Joomla directories with subsequent spawning of child processes (bash, cmd, sh) or outbound network connections from Apache/Nginx workers. Anomalous in normal Joomla operation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal patch compliance by 2026-06-19; standard practice is immediate asset scan. Article names 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor'—enumerate and remediate.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence Mechanism for Clipboard-Theft Malware
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'persistence and control'; article implies malware establishes lasting access via lightweight backdoor. No use case for detecting registry-based persistence unique to this family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Registry modifications under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, Runonce, or Services with anomalous value names or paths pointing to temporary directories, AppData subfolders, or obfuscated command lines. Cross-correlate with clipboard-access processes.

suggestion.title: Worm-like Propagation via Network Shares and Removable Media
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'worm-like propagation for persistence.' No detection rule targets lateral movement behavior typical of clipboard-theft malware self-replication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Executable or script files written to network shares (\\\\*\\C$, admin shares) or removable media by processes associated with clipboard theft. Look for self-replication patterns: same binary copied to multiple UNC paths or drive letters within minutes, followed by execution attempts.

suggestion.title: Wallet Address Replacement in Clipboard Before User Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'wallet replacement' attack. No detection rule monitors for clipboard content substitution prior to user paste events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor clipboard state changes correlating with crypto-wallet process activity. Detect overwrite of wallet addresses (long hex strings, base58-encoded Bitcoin/Ethereum addresses) in clipboard memory or clipboard history. Alert on multiple overwrites in short window.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Tampering with MDASH Security Integration Points
suggestion.rationale: Article states MDASH is 'integrating into real-world workflows across Windows, Azure, and identity systems' — attackers targeting these integration hooks for evasion is a direct corollary. Phrase 'real-world workflows' implies detectable persistence/callback patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution, registry modifications, or API calls targeting Windows Defender, Azure security services, or identity-system integration points. Flag unusual write access to security system binaries or configuration objects.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: Fingerprinting Agentic Security System Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'advancing security at AI speed' and discusses agentic decision-making — threat actors would probe these autonomous systems to learn detection thresholds, evasion windows, or decision logic. Article's focus on 'benchmark' improvements implies measurable detection behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure/Windows security endpoints for rapid-fire, exploratory API calls testing vulnerability detection responses or agentic system behavior. Flag patterns consistent with probing or benchmarking security detection logic.

suggestion.title: Execution: Exploitation of Agentic System Response Delays or Automation Gaps
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses agentic vulnerability detection and rapid response — attackers could attempt to race or saturate the agentic system with synthetic signals, queries, or malicious input to exploit automation latency or evade logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume, coordinated, or unusual-pattern API/process activity targeting vulnerability detection or Azure security endpoints. Detect attempts to generate false signals or overwhelm agentic response systems.

suggestion.title: XXE via parameter entity / OOB DNS callback pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'parameter-entity exfil' and OOB exfiltration in UC_7_5 but provides no hunt for the actual XXE parameter-entity XML syntax (e.g., `<!ENTITY % file SYSTEM 'file:///etc/passwd'>`). Phrase: 'XXE OOB / parameter-entity exfil'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for XML payloads posted to FHIR endpoints containing `<!ENTITY %` token sequences with SYSTEM declarations. Correlate with external DNS lookups from target FHIR process within 10s of POST. Parameter entities are specific to XXE-via-DTD attacks and reduce false positives vs. generic DOCTYPE detection.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable HAPI FHIR artifact deployment / library version check
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause in `XsltUtilities.saxonTransform()` method but does not specify patched version. Hunt should detect deployment/update of vulnerable HAPI FHIR JAR artifacts. Phrase: 'saxonTransform(...) overloads instead instantiate a **bare** `new ne…` (vulnerable code path).'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HAPI FHIR JAR creation/modification with version < [X] (requires CVE details for exact cutoff). Alert on tomcat/jboss deployments of vulnerable ca.uhn.hapi.fhir:hapi-fhir-* or net.sf.saxon:saxon-he artifacts. Early signal for vulnerable infrastructure.

suggestion.title: XXE via DOCTYPE expansion attack (Billion Laughs / XML bomb variant)
suggestion.rationale: UC_7_3 targets simple DOCTYPE payloads but not XML bomb / exponential entity expansion which bypasses some XXE filters. Article emphasizes the `saxonTransform` method has NO hardening—no entity expansion limits. Phrase: 'bare TransformerFactory' without 'FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to FHIR endpoints with Content-Length >> typical FHIR payload (>10MB) + nested entity definitions. Monitor FHIR Java process CPU/memory spikes coinciding with XML POST. XML bomb attacks consume process resources before XXE extraction payload runs.

suggestion.title: Successful XXE payload validation via server response exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes UC_7_4 (reading files) and UC_7_5 (OOB DNS) but omits in-band XXE where file contents are reflected in XSLT error messages or FHIR API response. Phrase: 'unable to resolve external entity' and transform failure messages leak file paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP 400/500 responses from FHIR endpoints where response body contains file paths (e.g., /etc/passwd) or unexpected XML structure. In-band XXE exfiltrates via error messages. Correlate POST request sender + response containing file content within same transaction.

suggestion.title: FHIR endpoint accepts XSLT stylesheet uploads / PUT with transform chain
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies both `transform(...)` and `saxonTransform(...)` are invoked via FHIR API but does not describe how attacker triggers the vulnerable method. Likely via PUT/POST with stylesheet reference. Phrase: 'XSLT transform helpers' exposed as FHIR endpoint operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FHIR endpoints for PUT/POST requests to paths containing 'transform', 'stylesheet', 'xslt', 'convert' or FHIR OperationDefinition endpoints that accept XML/XSLT parameters. Log the Content-Type and payload size. This identifies the entry point.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—this is the initial access footprint. Zero use cases generated to detect this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php?option=com_*) originating from unauthenticated sessions (no prior successful authentication for that IP in session logs). Alert on HTTP 200/302 responses for profile creation without valid auth tokens. Baseline legitimate admin activity; alert on external IP + successful creation patterns.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Widget Factory Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'upload and execution of PHP code' as the attack mechanism—no execution-phase detections generated despite this being the core exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multipart/form-data POST requests to editor/content upload endpoints with .php, .phtml, .php5 file extensions in payload. Correlate with subsequent HTTP GET requests to the uploaded file path from the same or different IP within seconds. Monitor WAF/IDS for PHP code tags in upload request bodies.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Detection: Rapid Editor Profile + PHP Upload
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain unifies unauthenticated access + immediate code upload. Article: 'unauthenticated users' enables both steps in sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect two-stage attack: unauthenticated POST to profile creation endpoint followed by file upload POST to the same Joomla instance within 30 seconds. Alert on HTTP 200/302 → 200 sequence from same external IP to the vulnerable Widget Factory Content Editor paths. Suppress false positives from batch admin operations (whitelist internal admin IP ranges).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Asset Inventory & Scanning
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active exploitation; no asset-exposure hunt for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor plugin presence/versions generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor plugin installations. Extract version numbers and match against CVE-2026-48907 vulnerable version ranges. Correlate with public-facing Joomla instances (internet-accessible IPs). Flag unpatched instances with federal due date 2026-06-19; escalate to CISO if exposed.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation PHP Execution Footprint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execution of PHP code' as the impact. No detection for post-upload execution monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server access logs for successful HTTP requests (200 responses) to suspicious paths (newly created files in /uploads/, /tmp/, /cache/ directories with .php extension). Correlate with PHP error logs for fatal/parse errors from those same files, indicating execution attempts. Alert if execution originates from external IP address matching the upload session.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Vulnerable Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-48907' and 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' explicitly; scanning for vulnerable plugin/version is canonical for CISA KEV entries. Article cites 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as recommended detection type.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Joomla installations with Widget Factory Content Editor plugin versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-48907. Cross-correlate asset inventory (CMDB, Shodan, internal scanner) with known-vulnerable versions. Federal due date 2026-06-19 creates urgency signal.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' as the attack vector. Profile creation by non-admin actors, especially unauthenticated, is anomalous and detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla Content Editor logs for profile creation attempts by unauthenticated users or non-privileged accounts. Alert on profile creation endpoint accessed before authentication or via default credentials.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Editor Profile Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles'. Uploads to editor directories are executable by design and represent direct code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file system events for .php or executable file writes to editor profile directories (typically /plugins/content/widget_* or similar). Pair with rapid subsequent web access to the upload directory to detect execution.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Editor Profile Path
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload and execution of PHP code'—execution is the terminal step of this attack. Web server processes executing PHP from unexpected paths indicate successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process spawning or web server child processes executing code from editor profile directories. Look for unusual PHP execution context (e.g., system commands, file I/O, network connects) initiated from Joomla Content Editor paths.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to asset-exposure hunt template and states CISA KEV vulnerabilities are actively exploited. Article: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [..._TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure].'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instances exposed on public-facing web servers. Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS responses containing Joomla editor version strings, framework signatures, or editor-specific endpoints. Correlate with vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-48907.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Joomla Editor Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated users' to create profiles and upload code: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated HTTP requests to Joomla editor creation/management endpoints. Monitor for 200/201 responses to profile creation endpoints when Authentication header is absent or invalid. Flag bulk or rapid requests to editor endpoints from single source.

suggestion.title: Joomla Editor Profile Creation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the intermediate step enabling exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual editor profile creation patterns: rapid succession of profile creations, profile creation from atypical source IPs, or profile creation with suspicious configuration attributes. Correlate with unauthenticated access logs.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' File upload is the payload mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP file uploads to Joomla content editor directories, especially those created post-profile instantiation. Flag uploads from unauthenticated sessions or following failed auth attempts. Correlate file upload events with subsequent PHP execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'execution of PHP code' following upload. This is the final exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP script execution (EXECUTE events, script_include logs, system() calls) in Joomla editor directories shortly after file upload events. Cross-reference with process creation logs for webserver child processes executing suspicious commands.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV inclusion confirms active exploitation. Detection should confirm whether CVE-2026-48907 patches are deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run authenticated vulnerability scan against Joomla installations for CVE-2026-48907 presence. Cross-reference with patch management records to identify systems with known vulnerable versions of Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes public-facing Joomla component with active exploitation (CISA KEV) and federal patch deadline 2026-06-19. Essential first hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Joomla installations with Widget Factory Content Editor component. Query web logs for requests to /components/com_contenteditor/ endpoints. Cross-reference against patch inventory to flag unpatched systems vulnerable to CVE-2026-48907.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase: 'unauthenticated users' + 'creation of new editor profiles.' This is the distinctive access pattern enabling the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/PUT requests to editor profile endpoints lacking valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Flag profile creation from external IP ranges or IPs with no prior Joomla activity.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Editor Profile Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' This is weaponization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for .php files written to editor profile directories during unauthenticated profile-creation operations. Correlate file timestamps with suspicious profile creation events in web application logs.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Uploaded Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Uploaded PHP code must execute to achieve impact. Article: 'execution of PHP code' establishes this execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP interpreter spawning child processes (bash, nc, curl, wget) with source file in editor profile directories. Flag unexpected system commands launched by www-data or web-server user processes.

suggestion.title: Web Service Reconnaissance Targeting Joomla Editor
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation reconnaissance of public-facing Joomla component. Article implies external scanning of vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Joomla admin paths and /components/com_contenteditor/ from external IPs with high 404 rate. Flag version-disclosure probes (e.g., /components/com_contenteditor/version.xml or manifest.xml requests).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-PHP Execution
suggestion.rationale: Execution phase typically followed by persistence/privilege escalation. Once PHP executes as web-server user, attackers pivot to system privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious PHP execution with subsequent privilege-escalation attempts (sudo, setuid calls, capability modifications) from web-server user. Flag sudo invocations from www-data or apache processes during exploit window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48907 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and confirms CISA KEV active exploitation status. Canonical asset-exposure hunt per article template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scan result matching CVE-2026-48907 against Joomla Content Editor assets. Prioritize public-facing instances; cross-reference patch dates against federal due-date 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack via 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Abnormal profile creation events indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla application logs for profile or editor-configuration creation from unauthenticated sessions. Alert on POST requests to profile-management endpoints without valid authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Web-Accessible Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code.' File uploads to web directories, especially .php extension, are exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php (or .phtml, .phar) file uploads to Joomla web-accessible paths (/components, /modules, /plugins). Correlate with unauthenticated POST requests. Legitimate uploads should show authenticated sessions; exploitation shows missing or invalid auth.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Web Server Process
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'execution of PHP code,' indicating RCE. Unexpected web server subprocess spawning or shell invocation reveals post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server process (apache2, php-fpm, nginx) for child processes spawning shells (/bin/bash, powershell.exe) or system commands (curl, wget, nc). Correlate timing with PHP file uploads and profile-creation events in web logs.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Package Name Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious package named 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt' was 'very similar to popular' legitimate package 'github.com/boltdb/bolt.' This attack vector requires detection of package uploads with names matching known packages within small edit distance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go package registry for newly-published packages with names within Levenshtein distance 1-2 of established packages. Flag when publisher has no prior commit history or owns no other packages. Cross-reference against CNCF/popular-packages lists.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Go Dependency Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes developers 'updating dependencies which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Detection should flag go.mod/go.sum resolution that pulls unexpected package versions or variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor 'go get' and 'go mod tidy' process execution. Alert when resolved package names differ from declared imports in source code or diverge from previous resolutions. Flag dependency downgrades to older 'cached' versions after removal announcements.

suggestion.title: Long-Dormant Cached Module Reactivation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching' allowed backdoor to 'go unnoticed for several years' before sudden access spike when developers updated. Detection should identify packages with old cache dates but recent sudden download volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate module proxy cache timestamp against download frequency. Alert on packages where downloads spike after long dormancy, especially post-vulnerability-disclosure dates. Flag packages without corresponding upstream GitHub releases or commits.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Backdoored Imports
suggestion.rationale: Article states backdoor 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' Network-layer detection should flag outbound C2 patterns from applications built with malicious dependency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS and TCP connections from binaries that statically link boltdb. Flag non-standard or IP-based C2 domains, high-frequency heartbeat patterns, or encrypted payloads from compiled Go applications built before module removal date (Feb 7, 2025).

suggestion.title: Binary Dependency Manifest Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes package 'reverted to actual legitimate version' but caching persisted malicious variant. Detection should identify compiled binaries where internal manifest (symbol tables, function signatures) differs from declared go.mod dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-build static analysis: extract Go.buildinfo from compiled binaries and cross-reference against go.mod/go.sum checksums. Alert when symbol signatures or function counts differ from expected package version, especially for packages with typo-adjacent names.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the direct attack vector—detection via web logs for POST/PUT to editor profile endpoints without valid session tokens or with guest/null user_id.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_joomlacontenteditor&task=profile.save) where authentication status is missing or user_id is null/guest. Baseline expected admin access and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Editor Profile Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'upload...of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Detection via file system or WAF logs for .php/.phtml extensions in POST bodies targeting editor profile creation endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag multipart form-data or POST request bodies containing .php, .phtml, .php3, .php5 file extensions when sent to editor profile endpoints. Cross-reference content-type and file headers to eliminate FPs (e.g., uploaded configs named .php but actually XML).

suggestion.title: PHP Process Execution from Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'execution of PHP code'—successful exploitation triggers PHP interpreter against attacker files. Detection via process creation logs showing php/php-cgi spawned with arguments referencing files in /uploads, /cache, /tmp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or php-cgi processes spawned as child of Apache/nginx where command line references .php files in writable directories. Correlate with profile creation events to identify root-cause timing.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Access Patterns to Editor Administrative Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation reconnaissance phase. Attackers probe for vulnerable Widget Factory editor endpoints via GET requests to /administrator paths. Article identifies specific component: 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GET requests to /administrator/index.php?option=com_joomlacontenteditor from external/non-whitelisted sources, or rapid sequential requests to editor paths from single source IP (component enumeration). Exclude known admin IPs via allowlist.

suggestion.title: Webshell / Reverse Shell Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase following successful PHP code upload. Article states impact is 'upload and execution'—attackers deploy persistent shells. Detection via web log anomalies (requests to newly-created .php with command-like parameters, or PHP spawning reverse connections).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor uploaded .php files for HTTP requests containing cmd=, shell=, or system() patterns in query strings. Alert on PHP processes spawning cmd.exe, bash, or initiating network connections to external IPs within minutes of profile upload events.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor CVE-2026-48907
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [..._TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure]. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline generated no use cases despite this clear directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instances exposed on public IPs or ports. Flag unpatched instances (patch due 2026-06-19) using CVE-2026-48907 signature. Alert on exposure discovery before federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow [...] creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'. No use case captures this access control bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor profile creation endpoints for requests from unauthenticated sessions (no valid session cookie, JWT absent, or explicit 'unauthenticated' marker in logs). Alert on successful profile creation responses from null-auth contexts.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Editor Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles'. Pipeline missed the upload delivery mechanism entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to editor profile creation endpoints containing PHP payloads (Content-Type application/octet-stream or multipart/form-data with .php extension, or inline PHP opening tags in payloads). Correlate with file creation events in web-root directories.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Child Process Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Upload and execution of PHP code will spawn child processes from the web server (apache, nginx, php-fpm). Article describes execution but no detection for post-exploitation process activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by web server processes (apache2, httpd, nginx, php-fpm) pointing to unexpected executables, especially shells (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe) or network tools (curl, wget, nc). Baseline known-good child processes per environment.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Directory Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article implies PHP execution from newly created profiles. Need to detect unexpected file creation in editor configuration or upload directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor editor profile directories (typically /components/com_*/media/profiles or /administrator/templates/*/profiles) for PHP file creation or modification by non-administrator accounts. Flag any .php files created after the vulnerability publication date (2026-06-16) in these paths.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Modification Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states "via Recovery Partition XML Files" — no detection use case generated despite this being the core attack surface. Should alert on unauthorized writes to recovery/boot partition XML configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation/modification events targeting paths like C:\Recovery\, EFI/ESP partitions, or boot configuration data files. Flag XML file writes from non-system processes or unsigned code to recovery partition. Correlate with BitLocker status changes.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Disable or Suspend Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit that "bypasses Windows BitLocker" — no detection for BitLocker tampering. Should catch manage-bde.exe calls, PowerShell encryption cmdlets, or WMI modifications to BitLocker policy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of manage-bde.exe with suspend/disable parameters, or calls to Win32_EncryptableVolume WMI class attempting property modifications. Include PowerShell commands invoking encryption-related cmdlets outside normal admin windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Direct Boot Sector or Recovery Partition Access
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly targets recovery partition via XML — no detection for raw disk I/O or direct \\Device\\HarddiskVolume access to boot/recovery regions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CreateFile calls with FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING or raw disk device paths (\\?\ prefix) targeting recovery volumes. Alert on processes calling Windows API functions like SetVolumeMountPoint or writing to non-standard partition offsets.

suggestion.title: GreatXML Exploit Artifact or Indicator Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names a specific exploit "GreatXML" — pipeline extracted zero artifact indicators. Should establish detections for exploit-specific file hashes, dropped payloads, C2 domains, or registry artifacts associated with this family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain intel feeds for GreatXML-related hashes, delivery domains, or command-line signatures. Alert on presence of known exploit samples, suspicious XML parsing utilities, or network beacons matching reported C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Boot Configuration Data (BCD) Registry Modification from User Process
suggestion.rationale: BitLocker bypass likely requires BCD alteration — no detection for suspicious HKLM\\BCD or boot policy registry writes from non-system processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry writes to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\BCD or WMI modifications to Win32_SystemBootConfiguration from processes outside System, csrss, or svchost. Include writes to REG_RESOURCE_REQUIREMENTS_LIST or EFI variables via user-mode code.

suggestion.title: Unexpected WMI Queries or MOF File Modifications Targeting Boot Objects
suggestion.rationale: BitLocker/recovery partition tampering often uses WMI — no detection for suspicious Win32_SystemBootConfiguration, Win32_EncryptableVolume, or MOF persistence attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WMI consumer/filter creation targeting boot-layer classes, MOF file drops to System32/wbem/, or ExecMethod calls on encryption or boot-partition objects. Alert if coming from user context or temporary locations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Joomla Content Editor Profile Creation — Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — the core improper access control. A successful exploitation must create a profile before uploading code. Web access logs should show POST/GET requests to profile creation endpoints from non-authenticated sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web access logs for requests to Joomla Content Editor profile creation endpoints (likely /component/contenteditor/profiles or similar) originating from unauthenticated sessions or IP addresses not in an allowed admin range. Flag any successful HTTP 200/302 responses that indicate profile creation without prior authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via Joomla Content Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code' — the exploitation mechanism. Detect file upload attempts to the vulnerable component containing PHP payloads or suspicious extensions (.php, .phtml, .php5).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs for multipart/form-data POST requests to editor upload endpoints containing PHP files or PHP code patterns (<?php, exec(), system(), passthru()). Correlate with file creation events showing .php files in web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor — Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV items are actively exploited; asset inventory is the first detection step. The article names the vulnerable product explicitly: 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internet-facing assets for instances of Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor plugin via version fingerprinting (HTTP header analysis, /README.md patterns, JavaScript file signatures). Cross-reference against CISA KEV due date 2026-06-19 to identify unpatched hosts.

suggestion.title: Web-Accessible PHP Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execution of PHP code' — after upload, the attacker must trigger execution. Monitor for new PHP processes spawned by the web server user or HTTP requests to newly uploaded files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution events where the parent is the web server process (apache, nginx, httpd, w3wp.exe) spawning suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, bash, sh, perl) or child processes with command lines containing common webshell patterns (whoami, id, cat /etc/passwd). Correlate with recent file uploads to web directories.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Endpoint Access Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: The improper access control allows unauthenticated access to editor functionality. Normal traffic patterns should show editor operations only from authenticated admin users. Article phrase: 'improper access control vulnerability'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authenticated editor profile modifications (from admin user accounts/IPs). Alert on requests to editor endpoints from non-admin sources, or requests lacking authentication session cookies/tokens that should be mandatory for this functionality.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries require remediation by federal due date and represent urgent patch priority. Article specifies CVE-2026-48907 as the identifier.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow... creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the initial exploitation vector and must be monitored at the application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (e.g., /administrator/index.php) from sources without valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Alert on profile creation with empty or default credentials.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via Joomla Editor Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Detection must capture the upload phase before execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file uploads to Joomla editor profile directories (/components/com_[editor_name]/profiles/ or similar) for PHP extensions or executable content. Alert on .php, .phtml, .php3+ files appearing in editor staging/upload directories.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Joomla Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'execution of PHP code' uploaded to editor profiles. Post-upload execution is the impact phase and highest-priority detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP process spawning or command execution originating from Joomla application directories, especially editor profile paths. Cross-reference HTTP request logs with process creation events to identify web-to-RCE chains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Editor Profile Creation Activity

suggestion.title: Suspicious Editor Profile Creation Without Authentication
