suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all CVE-2026-48907 matches in vulnerability management platform. Cross-correlate with patch logs to identify systems without applied vendor updates by federal due date 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: HTTP Access to Joomla com_joomcontenteditor Component
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' component — HTTP requests to this component path from untrusted sources indicate scanning or exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET/POST to /components/com_joomcontenteditor* or similar editor component paths from external IPs. 200 responses to unauthenticated requests signal exploitable misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Joomla Database Record Creation Without Admin Login
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'creation of new editor profiles' — successful attacks leave artifacts in joomla_extensions or joomla_profiles tables without corresponding admin session log entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate Joomla admin_logs for profile creation events with web_access_logs. Alert if profile is created without a corresponding authenticated admin session or if creation originates from public IP.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allow[s]... creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the canonical entry point; detecting profile creation without valid auth tokens is the primary control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT to Joomla Content Editor profile endpoints (e.g., /index.php?option=com_joomla_content_editor&task=profile*) where requests lack valid session cookies or authentication headers yet return 200/201 success (not 401/403). Baseline legitimate admin profile creation to tune false positives.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Editor Profile Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] upload... of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Detecting executable file uploads is essential to prevent execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multipart/form-data POST requests to editor profile creation endpoints containing files with .php, .phtml, .php7, or .phar extensions. Correlate with unauthenticated profile creation events. Segment alerts by authentication context to reduce false positives from legitimate admin uploads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanning Coverage
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status requires vulnerability scanning and patch compliance verification. Confirm scanners detect CVE-2026-48907 with Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor fingerprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate that vulnerability scanner includes CVE-2026-48907 detection (version fingerprinting for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor ≤ vulnerable version). Escalate any detections to high priority; correlate patch deployment against federal due date 2026-06-19 for compliance validation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code.' Detecting execution (not just upload placement) is necessary to catch active exploitation post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to newly-created editor profile file paths within 10 minutes of detected profile creation. Flag requests with high-entropy GET parameters (command injection indicators) or unusual User-Agents. Time-series correlation between creation and execution events is key to detection confidence.

suggestion.title: Rapid Multi-Profile Creation from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploiting the unauthenticated vulnerability may rapidly iterate or test multiple payloads. Plural 'profiles' in the article suggests enumeration/brute-force behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if a single source IP creates >3 editor profiles within 5 minutes, especially without authentication context. Baseline normal maintenance/admin activity to tune. Unauthenticated rapid profile creation is high-fidelity indicator of exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Go Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes github.com/botdb-go/bolt as typosquatting github.com/boltdb/bolt with malicious intent. 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' No detection for suspicious Go imports resembling popular packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go build processes and dependency resolution (go.mod, go.sum) for package names that are homoglyphs or near-matches to well-known modules (e.g., boltdb, gorm, etc.). Alert on first-time resolutions from untrusted module proxies or GitHub accounts that don't match the canonical maintainer. Cross-reference against Go module security databases.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Cache Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' and 'The Module was cached on Go Module Proxy, which continued to serve clients.' No detection for malicious modules persisting in cached proxy mirrors despite upstream removal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and alert on repeated Go module proxy requests (e.g., proxy.golang.org, pkg.go.dev) for package versions flagged in Go vulnerability database or recently removed from upstream repositories. Detect when developers update go.mod to pinned versions known to be backdoored (e.g., github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1).

suggestion.title: Command and Control via Compromised Go Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article states the backdoor 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' No detection for C2 communications initiated by Go processes or unusual outbound network activity from build/runtime environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from Go processes (go.exe, compiled binaries from recent builds) to non-standard ports or external domains not in allowed-list. Alert on DNS resolutions to low-reputation domains or IPs from processes pulling packages from module proxies. Correlate with recent go.mod changes.

suggestion.title: Software Supply Chain Dependency Update to Backdoored Version
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Organizations updating BoltDB to v1.3.1 (released Nov 2021, cached in proxy until Jan 2025) should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect changes to go.mod/go.sum or package.json that pin or upgrade to known-backdoored versions (cross-reference against Go CVE database and Snyk alerts). Alert specifically on go get github.com/botdb-go/bolt or similar typosquatted packages in build logs. Flag any organization with go.sum entries for v1.3.1 or recent updates to that version after Jan 30, 2025 discovery date.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Package Name Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack method: 'Typo squatting attacks happen when bad actors create and upload harmful software packages to online libraries using names very similar to popular ones.' No generic detection for new package uploads with names resembling high-value targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository upload events and new package registrations (Go, NPM, PyPI, Nuget) for Levenshtein distance or character-similarity matches against top-100 packages in each ecosystem. Alert on new accounts or first-time publishers uploading near-homoglyph names. Combine with reputation scoring (new account, unusual upload cadence, zero documentation).

Baseline legitimate profile creation IP/user patterns and alert on anomalies.

Cross-reference with web server logs for subsequent GET/POST requests to newly created .php files.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states exploit 'Bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files'—the core attack mechanism is XML tampering in restricted boot/recovery areas. No use case was generated for this foundational IOA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, modification, or write events targeting recovery partition paths (\Recovery\, \EFI\, System32\Recovery\) with .xml extension. Flag if process lacks system integrity or runs from user-writable directory. Correlate with subsequent boot-time behavior changes or BitLocker state queries.

suggestion.title: GreatXML Exploit Execution and Variants
suggestion.rationale: Named exploit 'GreatXML' in title provides explicit IOC foundation; pipeline should generate process-execution detection against this exploit name and related command-line patterns. Absence indicates failure to extract named-threat indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process spawning containing 'GreatXML' identifier, XML parsing utilities targeting recovery paths (msbuild.exe, powershell.exe), or scripting engines with XML/config file arguments. Flag unsigned executables or execution from %TEMP%, Downloads, or AppData user-writable paths.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Metadata and Recovery Key Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploit's mechanism is BitLocker bypass via recovery partition tampering—should detect unauthorized WMI queries, registry enumeration, or file reads of BitLocker recovery credentials or configuration metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WMI namespace queries (Win32_EncryptableVolume, Win32_Volume), registry reads of HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\TPM or \Security\Encryption, or file access to %SystemRoot%\System32\Recovery\*. Escalate if requestor is non-admin or scripts are involved.

suggestion.title: Boot Configuration or EFI Boot Order Modification
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partition XML files are typically parsed at boot time; successful exploitation likely results in modifications to boot sequence, EFI variables, or BCD (Boot Configuration Data). Article title implies persistence post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to BCD registry hive, EFI boot variables, or bootloader configuration files (bootmgr, winload.efi). Flag unsigned code writes to System32\hal.dll or Drivers\. Correlate temporally with recovery partition XML writes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation or Token Impersonation for Restricted Partition Access
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partitions are access-restricted; exploiting requires privilege escalation or kernel-level access. Article doesn't detail mechanism, but UCA should detect pre-exploitation privilege-gain attempts or BYOVD/kernel exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CreateRemoteThread or SetWindowsHookEx to system processes, UAC bypass patterns, or parent-child process chains where low-privilege process spawns token-elevated child. Flag execution of exploitation frameworks or BYOVD candidates (vulnerable drivers, WMI class loading).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-write events (PHP files created in web-accessible directories like /components, /modules) with subsequent PHP process spawning from web-server user context (www-data, apache). Alert on execution of recently-written files or unusual PHP process parents.

suggestion.title: Suspicious or Rapid Editor Profile Creation in Joomla
suggestion.rationale: Attacker persistence mechanism: 'creation of new editor profiles' for ongoing access. Should detect account-creation abuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla user/profile creation logs for bulk or rapid creation events (>5 profiles per minute), profiles created outside business hours, or profiles with administrative privilege assigned. Flag profiles created without corresponding authenticated admin session audit trail.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — this is the attack vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php or component paths) that lack authentication tokens, session IDs, or originate from unauthenticated contexts. Look for HTTP 200/201 responses indicating successful profile creation without prior login activity.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Joomla Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code' — critical post-exploitation step. No detection for file-upload activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP file writes to web-accessible directories via Joomla editor components. Flag requests to profile/editor endpoints followed by .php file creation in upload directories, or PHP process spawning from web-server user context with PHP file arguments pointing to recently-created uploads.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt — Joomla Widget Factory Content Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs to run asset-exposure hunt for CVE-2026-48907 against fleet. Pipeline omitted entirely.

suggestion.title: Joomla Component Access Without Authentication

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to /administrator/index.php, component endpoints, or editor-related URLs that receive successful responses (2xx/3xx) but originate from sessions with no prior authentication activity. Flag rapid-fire requests to multiple administrative paths from single source.

suggestion.title: Joomla Editor Profile Enumeration

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated HTTP requests to editor/profile-related URIs (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_*editor* or similar patterns) with 404/403 responses followed by 200 responses, indicating successful endpoint discovery and exploitation by same source.

suggestion.title: Unexpected PHP Execution from Web Upload Directories

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PHP process spawning with command-line arguments referencing recently-created files in /uploads, /tmp, or /media directories. Correlate with web-server process (apache, nginx, php-fpm user) and absent legitimate deployment activity.

suggestion.title: CodeIgniter4 application fingerprinting via HTTP signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes CodeIgniter4 is the target but provides no recon-phase hunt. Framework exposes itself through error pages, X-Powered-By headers, and URL route structure (/index.php/controller/method). Article states vulnerability affects CodeIgniter4 specifically—reconnaissance should precede exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP responses containing CodeIgniter4 identifiers: X-Powered-By: CodeIgniter headers, debug-toolbar markers, or characteristic error page text. Also identify URL patterns matching CodeIgniter4's routing (/index.php routes or specific path structures).

suggestion.title: File upload validation rule bypass: MIME-extension mismatch on ext_in rule
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'The ext_in upload validation rule checked the MIME-derived guessed extension instead of the client-provided filename extension.' This is the vulnerability's exact mechanism but no UC hunts CodeIgniter4 validation logs where MIME-detected type diverges from actual filename extension on the same file.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: CodeIgniter4 validation logs should record when ext_in rule processes uploads. Hunt for entries where detected MIME extension differs from filename extension on the same upload event—successful bypass leaves the file in place with both mismatches present.

suggestion.title: Image magic bytes + PHP code pattern in uploaded file
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'shell.php containing GIF-like content.' No UC hunts file-content signature mismatch: files with image headers (GIF87a/89a, FFD8FF for JPEG) that simultaneously contain PHP code markers like `<?php`, `eval()`, or shell execution functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor uploaded files in web-accessible directories for polyglot content: image file signatures (first bytes = GIF8, FFD8, 89504E47) combined with code patterns (`<?php`, `eval(`, `system(`, `passthru()`, backticks). This is the exact masquerading shape described.

suggestion.title: Joomla POST to Admin Endpoints from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated profile creation implies POST to an editor/admin endpoint without valid session cookie. Detect baseline-anomalous POST traffic to admin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests to Joomla /administrator, /index.php?option=com_*, or editor profile endpoints that lack valid authenticated session cookie or include Cookie: JSESSIONID=<empty/default>. Include requests that receive 200 after prior 403.

suggestion.title: Profile Creation Parameter Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Improper access control suggests parameter tampering or missing authorization checks on profile creation API. Detect requests with suspicious profile-creation payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/GET requests containing profile creation parameters (e.g., profile_name, profile_type, editor_type, permission_level) originating from IPs/users without known admin/editor role assignment. Detect requests with privilege-escalation indicators (e.g., permission=admin, role=super).

suggestion.title: Typo-squatted Go Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the typo-squatting attack: 'similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt' vs malicious 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt'. This is the initial-access vector that must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod and go.sum files, as well as package manager logs, for installations of github.com/botdb-go/bolt or other transposition-based package variants (bdb vs boltdb, botdb vs boltdb). Alert on any version 1.3.1 or installation timestamps between November 2021 and January 2025.

suggestion.title: Go Module Cache Poisoning Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack mechanism: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' — the module 'stayed in the system for 3 years'. Cache pollution is the persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when Go module proxy caches serve module github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1 across clients. Monitor for cache hit spikes on typo-squatted package variants. Alert if a cached module version predates all current security advisories for that package family.

suggestion.title: C2 Outbound Beaconing from Go Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article states the backdoor 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server'. C2 communication is the command-and-control phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound network connections from Go applications (verified via binary metadata or container inspection) to external C2 infrastructure. Focus on connections from processes loading the compromised BoltDB v1.3.1 dependency. Flag regular periodic connections to non-standard ports or known malicious domains.

suggestion.title: Bulk Dependency Update Triggering Malicious Version Install
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years'. Mass updating of Go modules unknowingly pulled the malicious cached version into production.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk go.mod updates that downgrade or change package source to typo-squatted variants (e.g., adding github.com/botdb-go/bolt when previous version was github.com/boltdb/bolt). Alert on updates pulling versions older than current security baseline for supply chain packages.

suggestion.title: Package Name Similarity Masquerading Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: typo-squatting relies on name confusion. Article states attacker 'hope people will mistakenly download and install these dangerous versions'. Need to detect uploads of packages with transposition-distance ≤2 from popular packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go Module Proxy and GitHub for new package releases with names differing from established packages by single-character transpositions, dropped characters, or homograph substitutions (bdb vs boltdb, botdb vs boltdb). Flag for manual review when levenshtein distance is ≤2 from known popular packages.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor CVE-2026-48907 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation. Article states 'observed exploited in the wild' yet zero asset-discovery use case generated. This is the foundational hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory and vulnerability scanner for unpatched Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor installations. Identify CVE-2026-48907 detections on assets with public-facing web exposure, prioritize by internet-facing status.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—this is the authentication bypass vector. Completely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla editor profile creation endpoints for requests without valid session/authentication tokens. Detect POST requests to profile management URIs (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_joomlacontenteditor) with missing or tampered Authorization headers.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Web-Accessible Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code' but execution phase is completely absent from kill chain. Must detect malicious file write.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php/.phtml file writes to Joomla web-accessible directories (components, media, plugins) correlated with unauthenticated editor profile creation in preceding minutes. Flag suspicious PHP code in uploads (system(), exec(), passthru() calls).

suggestion.title: PHP Execution via Uploaded File
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execution of PHP code'—no execution-phase detections provided. Must detect runtime command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php/php-cgi child processes spawned by web server (apache2, nginx, httpd) with execution of recently-written PHP files in web-accessible paths. Alert on suspicious system commands invoked from PHP context.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence in Joomla Installation
suggestion.rationale: Uploaded and executed PHP code naturally persists as a web shell. Article describes execution capability but no persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for newly-created PHP files in Joomla directories with timestamps matching exploitation window. Scan content for web shell indicators (eval(), base64_decode(), $_REQUEST execution, one-liner command handlers).

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Pattern Against Joomla Admin Panel
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires accessing editor functionality without credentials. Article emphasizes 'improper access control'—detect authentication-bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track successful requests to Joomla editor endpoints without prior successful administrator login. Detect rapid, automated profile-creation requests from single IP/user-agent (behavior consistent with CVE exploitation tooling).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to Joomla profile/editor creation endpoints (administrator/index.php, plugin manager) from unauthenticated sessions (guest user, no prior login event). Alert on successful 200/302 responses to profile creation followed by file writes in the same session.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Editor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via...editor profiles.' Uploaded .php files to web-accessible directories are the execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .php file creation in /components/com_*/editor/*, /plugins/editors/*, /media/editors/*, or equivalent Joomla editor paths, within 5 minutes of unauthenticated profile creation POST. Correlate source IP across HTTP access logs and file change events.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution in Joomla Editor Context
suggestion.rationale: Article documents active wild exploitation (CISA KEV status), so uploaded PHP code must be executed. Process-level detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for php.exe or php-cgi process spawned by web server user (www-data, apache, iis apppool) with parent/CWD referencing plugins or editors. Monitor Joomla application logs for unexpected extension activation or task execution from editor components.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly prescribes: 'CVE-2026-48907 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline must generate scanner-driven detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instances with versions in CVE-2026-48907 affected range. Prioritize internet-facing assets (public IP, no WAF). Cross-reference scanner match timestamp with netflow/Zeek for successful inbound remote connections.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin/Editor Feature Access Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'improper access control' allows unauthenticated users to access admin/profile creation features. Authorization bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla logs for admin task execution (task=save, action=create, component operations) from guest/anonymous users. HTTP proxy should show direct /administrator/ access with zero prior successful authentication from that IP in the session window.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — this is the primary access control bypass vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla access logs for POST/PUT requests to editor profile endpoints (e.g., component=com_editors, task=profile operations) arriving without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Alert on profile creation attempts originating from external IP ranges or non-administrative user contexts.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Joomla Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly includes 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles' — file upload to web-accessible directories is the execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application logs for multipart file uploads to Joomla plugin/editor directories (e.g., /plugins, /components/com_editors/). Alert on .php, .phtml files written to web root with timestamps outside maintenance windows. Track file size anomalies in profile uploads (large binaries in profile data).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Widget Factory Component Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due date 2026-06-19; vulnerability scanning is baseline detection for known-exploited vulnerabilities regardless of patch claims, due to industry patch lag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor presence and version matching CVE-2026-48907 signature. Cross-reference asset inventory to flag public-facing Joomla instances. Generate high-priority alerts for unpatched instances with internet-routable IPs; escalate based on federal timeline.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Unauthenticated Requests to Joomla Administrator Functions
suggestion.rationale: Improper access control means attackers bypass authentication; monitor for abnormal request patterns to normally-restricted endpoints as described in 'unauthenticated' profile creation capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTP request patterns to /administrator, editor profile endpoints, and component configuration pages — establish threshold for authenticated-only traffic. Alert on sustained requests from external/untrusted sources lacking authentication context. Correlate with failed login logs and IP reputation data.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Access and Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Recovery Partition XML Files' as attack surface: 'Bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-system access to Windows recovery/EFI partitions (\Recovery, \EFI, \BOOT, \BIOS) by non-system processes, or CREATE/MODIFY operations on .xml files within those paths. Alert on process elevation followed by XML file access in recovery contexts, or on attempts to mount recovery partitions via diskpart, SetupAPI, or direct partition access.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Metadata Enumeration and Key Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'Bypasses Windows BitLocker'. Recovery partition XML files store BitLocker metadata and key material. Article: 'GreatXML Exploit Bypasses Windows BitLocker'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process calls to manage-bde.exe, WMI BitLocker methods (win32_encryptablevolume), or direct reads of BitLocker configuration registry hives (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\BitLocker). Flag recovery key export or enumeration attempts, or access to recovery XML files by processes not signed by Microsoft.

suggestion.title: Privileged XML Processing in Pre-OS/Recovery Context
suggestion.rationale: Threat name 'GreatXML' and attack chain require XML parsing during recovery/pre-OS execution with elevated privilege. Article: 'GreatXML Exploit ... XML Files'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of XML parsers (powershell.exe, cscript.exe, mshta.exe, msxml3-6 library loads) with SYSTEM or TrustedInstaller privileges when processing files from recovery partitions or boot-time execution contexts. Flag unusual XML parser invocations from System32 that read recovery-related paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Recovery Partition Mount and Direct Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires access to recovery partition normally sealed from user-mode code. 'Recovery Partition XML Files' implies partition enumeration, mounting, or direct access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-OS processes invoking volume/partition APIs (SetupAPI, VDS/VSS, diskpart.exe, ioctl calls), attempting to enumerate or mount recovery partitions, or accessing raw partition tables. Flag processes acquiring SeSystemtimePrivilege or SeLoadDriverPrivilege that interact with recovery partition paths.

suggestion.title: XML External Entity (XXE) Attack on BitLocker Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partition XML files likely encode BitLocker configuration, key material, or encryption metadata. XXE or XML bomb exploitation is congruent with 'GreatXML' naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for XML parsing exceptions or resource exhaustion (billion laughs attacks, entity expansion loops) when XML parsers consume files from recovery/boot partitions. Alert on external entity (DOCTYPE/ENTITY) declarations in XML files recovered from recovery partitions, or on parser errors indicative of XXE attempts.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Editor — Unauthenticated Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_contenteditor) from unauthenticated sessions or sessions lacking admin privileges. Baseline: legitimate profile creation should be rare or nonexistent in typical environments.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via Joomla Editor Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code.' This is the payload delivery and T1505.004 (Web Shell) execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for multipart/form-data HTTP requests with .php, .phtml, or executable extensions being written to web-accessible directories via the editor profile creation endpoint. Flag unexpected executable file uploads to /media, /images, or web root followed by HTTP requests to execute the uploaded file.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires federal remediation by 2026-06-19 (same-day deadline). Scanner detection is primary IOC for asset prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any CVE-2026-48907 match in vulnerability scanner results for Joomla instances, especially those with internet-facing administrative interfaces. Prioritize for emergency patching ahead of 2026-06-19 deadline.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Plugin Presence on Joomla Instances
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires the vulnerable plugin to be installed. Asset discovery of affected software is prerequisite for hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Joomla installations running Widget Factory Content Editor via plugin manifest enumeration (HTTP GET to plugin paths, plugin XML responses, HTTP headers). Flag unpatched versions in asset inventory for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution Post-Upload to Joomla
suggestion.rationale: After PHP file is uploaded via unauthenticated editor profile creation, attacker executes it. Correlation between upload and execution signals exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST requests to editor profile endpoints with subsequent HTTP requests to newly-created PHP files. Look for .php files in web root with recent creation timestamps matching upload requests, then accessed via HTTP GET/POST within seconds. This signals web shell execution.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability affects 'public-facing application' and CISA KEV only lists actively exploited flaws. Standard first-line hunt for exposed Joomla + Content Editor installations. Article: 'public-facing application'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Joomla installations with Content Editor plugin active. Use asset discovery scanners (e.g., Shodan, Censys) for 'Joomla' + 'Content Editor' headers, HTTP fingerprints, or plugin signatures. Correlate with internal vulnerability scanner CVE-2026-48907 findings. Prioritize publicly routable assets.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — this is the attack entry point. Detection should flag profile creation from non-authenticated sessions before successful login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php or /component/contenteditor/profiles). Alert when requests originate from unauthenticated sessions (no valid session token, IP not in whitelist, user-agent anomalies). High FP risk from legitimate admin use — baseline typical profile creation patterns first.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Joomla Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Detection must capture the actual payload delivery (PHP file upload) separate from profile creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file write events to Joomla Content Editor upload directories for .php extensions. Cross-correlate with process execution of PHP interpreter (php-cgi, php-fpm) immediately after upload. Baseline expected PHP uploads from admin users; flag all others. Watch for polyglot uploads (.php.jpg) as bypass.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Exploitation Pattern — Joomla Content Editor
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalog entry requires active threat hunting for this specific CVE. Article: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Standard practice is cross-fleet scanner correlation + intrusion attempt detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all hosts in vulnerability scanner output with CVE-2026-48907 present. Cross-correlate with patch management system to identify unpatched instances. Secondary: hunt logs for exploitation signatures (malformed profile creation requests, PHP error logs from editor component, unexpected PHP execution from web-accessible paths).

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Joomla Editor — Post-Exploit Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful exploitation results in 'execution of PHP code' on server. Post-exploitation detection must cover attacker activity post-upload (webshell runtime, reverse shell, data exfil).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP process spawning unexpected child processes (bash, cmd.exe, powershell) immediately after Content Editor uploads. Alert on outbound network connections from php-cgi/php-fpm to non-whitelisted external IPs. Look for PHP sessions with abnormally long runtimes or memory allocation anomalies in application logs.

suggestion.title: Scanner/WAF Detection: CVE-2026-48907 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation flow can be detected at ingress before profile creation succeeds. Article: 'improper access control' is the vulnerability class — WAF rules should detect unauthenticated attempts to access restricted endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: WAF signature-based detection for POST/GET requests to /component/contenteditor/profiles/* or /administrator/index.php?option=com_contenteditor&... from unauthenticated sources. Alert on 403->success state transitions (access control bypass). IDS rule: flag unusual HTTP methods or Content-Type headers targeting editor plugin paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation via Joomla Widget Factory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated users' can perform 'creation of new editor profiles'—this is the initial exploitation step and should be detectable via POST/create requests to editor endpoints without valid authentication tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor profile-creation endpoints (typical paths: /plugins/system/widget_factory/*, /components/com_widget_factory/*, /administrator/index.php?option=com_*) from sources without valid session/authentication cookies. Baseline legitimate profile creation and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Web-Accessible Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload... of PHP code'—profile creation likely accepts file uploads that are written to web-accessible paths. Detect uploads of .php files or suspicious content-type mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file writes to Joomla web directories (typically /images/*, /media/*, /tmp/*, /components/*, /plugins/*) that correlate with preceding editor profile creation attempts. Correlate web server logs showing POST uploads with subsequent file-system writes.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Editor Profile Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'execution of PHP code' via newly created profiles—web server must execute PHP files uploaded to profile storage. Detect web process spawning child processes or executing code patterns indicative of PHP execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to uploaded profile paths (GET/POST to recently written .php files in editor directories) followed by unexpected child-process execution (typical for PHP shell: curl, wget, bash, powershell spawned by php or httpd processes).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scan Detection & Patch Gap
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry implies active exploitation in the wild—standard hunt is asset exposure. Article provides CVE identifier and federal patch due-date (2026-06-19) which should drive patch urgency hunts and scanner correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48907 against live web services inventory. Identify hosts running Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor versions ≤ [vulnerable version] without patches. Correlate with web-server logs for any access attempts to known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Improper Access Control: Unauthorized Access to Joomla Editor Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'improper access control' allowing unauthenticated access to editor features—detect requests to admin/protected editor endpoints from IPs/users lacking valid authorization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200/302 responses to Joomla editor configuration endpoints (/administrator/*, /backend/*, /editor/config*) from requests lacking valid session cookies, API keys, or authentication headers. Flag rapid iteration through editor endpoints as scanning behavior.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Plugin Activation & Suspicious Component Access
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' as the vulnerable product—detect deployment, activation, or suspicious interaction with this plugin/component as precursor to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on web requests to Widget Factory component paths (/components/com_widget_factory/*, plugin_widget_factory* files) especially POST/PUT requests or high-volume GET requests from unusual sources. Correlate with file-system changes in plugin/component directories.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Unauthenticated Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the weaponization step and entry point; no use case generated for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla Content Editor profile endpoints (/administrator/index.php?option=com_contenteditor or variant) originating from unauthenticated sessions (no valid admin token/session ID). Alert on HTTP 200/201 responses to profile creation requests from non-whitelisted source IPs or unusual User-Agents.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Web-Accessible Media Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code'—detection must capture the upload stage. No use case exists for file-write patterns after profile creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP-executable file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .phtml) created in Joomla /media or Content Editor plugin directories within 5 minutes of an unauthenticated profile creation HTTP request. Cross-reference creator process context (should be web service account, not admin user).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies execution occurs after upload: 'execution of PHP code via...creation of new editor profiles.' Detect process spawning (PHP interpreter invocation) or HTTP request execution of the uploaded payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Windows: detect w3wp.exe, httpd.exe, or nginx.exe spawning php.exe / php-cgi.exe with command-line referencing files in /media subdirectories. Linux: detect Apache/Nginx child processes spawning php-fpm with suspicious working directory or script arguments. Correlate process creation time with file creation timestamp.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using template and CVE substitution. Pipeline failed to instantiate the template logic for this active-exploitation CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48907 in Joomla Content Editor installations. Cross-reference against CMDB / patch-management records to identify systems with contradicting patch status (reported patched but still flagged). Prioritize internet-facing/DMZ instances. Validate federal due-date enforcement (2026-06-19 remediation deadline).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation PHP Web Shell Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution' without limitation—adversary may establish long-lived web shell. No persistence-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated HTTP requests to the same uploaded PHP file from multiple source IPs or scheduled/recurring request patterns. Alert on creation of additional files in the same directory by the web service account post-exploitation. Detect outbound traffic (C2 callbacks) from the web service account spawned after suspicious PHP execution.

suggestion.title: Joomla Editor Profile Creation by Unauthenticated Users
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — unauthorized profile creation is the earliest direct exploitation signal and distinguishes this from generic web scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests to Joomla editor profile endpoints (e.g., index.php?option=com_editorprofile&task=profile) originating without valid session cookies or Authorization headers, particularly if followed by 200-series responses. Cross-reference with failed authentication logs to isolate pre-auth attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Upload to Joomla Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles' — detecting PHP writes to editor paths is post-auth-bypass, pre-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful HTTP POST to editor plugin directories returning 200 status, correlated with new .php file creation in Joomla editor plugin paths (e.g., /components/com_editorprofile/, /plugins/editors/). Focus on timeline proximity (upload → file-write within <5 seconds).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Joomla Widget Factory Editor Plugin Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' as the vulnerable software; asset inventory is the preventive layer before exploitation window opens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Joomla installations with Widget Factory editor plugin active (CVE-2026-48907 match). Cross-reference scanner version strings against patch-management DB to isolate unpatched or no-compliance instances. Enumerate via Joomla administrator panel or plugin-listing endpoints.

suggestion.title: PHP Command Execution in Joomla Editor Plugin Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution' — post-upload execution detection captures actual code-run phase. Execution should occur in web-server process context with editor plugin in working directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP interpreter (php.exe, php-cgi, php-fpm child processes) spawned by web server workers with working directory or process arguments containing Joomla editor plugin paths. Alert on unexpected shell metacharacters or system-command child processes (cmd, bash, powershell) spawned from PHP in these contexts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in template, substitute CVE-2026-48907.' Pipeline generated zero use cases and ignored explicit template guidance. CISA KEV due-date is 2026-06-19 — detection is urgent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner signatures or HTTP fingerprints identifying Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor with CVE-2026-48907. Prioritize remediation by federal due-date. Use asset-exposure template with substitution of CVE-2026-48907 in both Splunk and Defender KQL.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability permits 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the attack vector; profile creation without session should be detectable and alertable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla access logs for editor profile creation (POST/PUT to profile endpoints) originating from requests with no valid authentication token. Correlate request source, profile name, and timestamp for post-exploitation pivoting.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Editor Components
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability enables 'upload and execution of PHP code.' Pipeline missed detection for the upload phase and subsequent execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification events (.php files) in Joomla editor component directories (typically /components/com_joomlaeditor/profiles/). Correlate with HTTP requests to the same paths from unauthenticated or suspicious sources.

suggestion.title: Joomla Web Shell Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: 'Execution of PHP code' is the stated impact. Detection of actual web shell execution (eval, system, exec, passthru calls) is a natural hunt for post-compromise analysis that pipeline omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt PHP execution logs for shell metacommands (system(), shell_exec(), exec(), passthru()) originating from Joomla editor component paths. Detect HTTP requests to newly-created .php files with abnormal query parameters or POST payloads.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance for Joomla Editor Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV active exploitation suggests scanning/reconnaissance phase. Pipeline missed detection for fuzzing or enumeration of Joomla editor management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on patterns of HTTP 404/403 responses or parameter fuzzing against Joomla editor component paths. High volume of requests to non-existent profiles, permission-denied editor operations, or repeated failed authentication attempts to editor admin interfaces indicate scanning.

suggestion.title: Upload validation rule bypass: file extension mismatch on MIME-derived filename
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the vulnerability mechanism: 'ext_in upload validation rule checked the MIME-derived guessed extension instead of the client-provided filename extension.' Pipeline missed detection for the validation-bypass itself, not just post-exploitation. Could detect via form-data inspection or upload-handler logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multipart form submissions where Content-Type and filename extension are mismatched (e.g., Content-Type: image/gif but filename ends in .php/.phtml). If upload logs or proxy can capture multipart body metadata, flag discrepancies between declared MIME type and actual file extension.

suggestion.title: Recently-uploaded file retroactively executed by web server
suggestion.rationale: Article workflow: file uploaded, then web server spawns shell FROM that file. Detection should correlate file creation timestamp in upload directory with immediate subsequent process execution. Pipeline UC_102_1 and UC_102_3 are separate; this joins them.

suggestion.title: PHP File Creation in Joomla Editor Directories

suggestion.title: Invocation of Newly Uploaded PHP in Joomla Editor Paths

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence in Joomla Editor Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PHP upload capability enabling persistence. Uploaded PHP files survive and remain executable for future exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated POST to Joomla Editor Profile Endpoints

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via Joomla Editor Profile

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Editor Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV categorization means active exploitation; article identifies Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor as vulnerable product with federal patch due date 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Profile Creation Attempts

Flag POST/PUT requests to profile creation endpoints without valid auth tokens, session cookies, or CSRF tokens.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Editor Directories

suggestion.title: Suspicious Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate 'auth-user: service-brother' traffic (expected destination IPs, ports, endpoints, request methods). suggestion.rationale: Truncating files is a defense-evasion tactic to destroy logs or audit trails. Article identifies file truncation as a direct attack capability; insufficient focus on intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TRUNCATE operations in PostgreSQL targeting log tables or audit tables, or file truncation commands (e.g., > redirection) against Splunk logs, audit logs, or system logs from the sidecar process context.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access Attempt

Flag requests that lack valid authentication tokens, session identifiers, or certificates. Correlate external IP source address with baseline of legitimate internal/service-to-service sidecar communication.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Arbitrary File Truncation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows attackers to 'truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. File truncation via this service is the direct exploitation impact.

Establish baseline of legitimate truncation during maintenance and alert on out-of-band truncations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Arbitrary File Creation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'create...arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. File creation is the second exploitation primitive and potential foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation in critical Splunk paths (bin/, etc/, var/lib/) that correlate temporally with unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access. Flag files with suspicious ownership, unusual extensions (.sh, .exe, .psm1 in config dirs), or created outside standard deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar External Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies this as CISA KEV ('currently being exploited') and recommends asset-exposure hunt. Sidecar endpoint must be identified as reachable from untrusted networks without authentication enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances with exposed PostgreSQL sidecar service ports reachable from external networks. Verify instances respond to unauthenticated connection attempts; any successful unauthenticated session to sidecar indicates vulnerability. Cross-reference with patch status to find unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Two-Stage Exploitation: Sidecar Access + File Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Complete kill-chain detection: unauthenticated sidecar access followed by file creation/truncation. Sequential correlation reduces false positives and confirms exploitation intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated network request to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (from external/untrusted IP, no valid auth) immediately followed (within 1–60 seconds) by file truncation or creation in Splunk-managed directories. This two-stage pattern directly indicates CVE-2026-20253 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated POST/GET to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Core attack vector; zero UCs generated despite explicit description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints (typically non-standard high-numbered ports) without valid authentication headers or session tokens. Alert on 200/201 responses to POST/GET operations from external or untrusted IPs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create...arbitrary files.' Exploitation indicator omitted from pipeline output despite being explicit attack capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation initiated from PostgreSQL sidecar process context, or file creations in directories outside Splunk's configured base paths. Cross-reference with unauthenticated sidecar request timelines.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation on Splunk Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'truncate arbitrary files.' Destructive action not represented in any UC; direct impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on truncate/delete operations on Splunk config, dashboard, or data files. Correlate with sidecar endpoint access to separate legitimate admin activity from exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-20253 and CISA KEV status indicates active wild exploitation. Pipeline generated zero vulnerability IOCs or scanner signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Splunk Enterprise instances with unresolved CVE-2026-20253. Flag any instances unpatched after federal due date 2026-06-21. Correlate with network anomalies on sidecar ports.

suggestion.title: POST /crawl* with launcher-switch keywords in request body (body-aware variant)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Docker API server accepted a request-supplied browser_config.extra_args, which flowed into Chromium's launch arguments.' Payload is JSON in POST body, not query string. Original UC_3_2 searches wrong field entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /crawl, /crawl/stream, /crawl/job where request body JSON contains 'extra_args' or 'browser_config' fields with values matching Chromium launcher-switch patterns (--utility-cmd-prefix, --renderer-cmd-prefix, --gpu-launcher, --browser-subprocess-path).

suggestion.title: Chromium process with --no-zygote AND subprocess-launcher flag co-occurrence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'inject Chromium switches that replace a child-process launch command...together with --no-zygote, causing Chromium to fork/exec.' The --no-zygote flag is the attack enabler (disables zygote sandboxing); co-occurrence with launcher-override flags is telltale and extremely rare in legitimate Chromium usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single Chromium process event with simultaneous --no-zygote AND at least one of {--utility-cmd-prefix, --renderer-cmd-prefix, --gpu-launcher, --browser-subprocess-path}. This tuple is near-pathognomonic for this exploit.

suggestion.title: Docker/Kubernetes API access to Crawl4AI endpoint (container-aware context)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Docker API server' and vulnerability is specific to containerized deployment. Detection should correlate suspicious API calls with container infrastructure context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST to Crawl4AI /crawl* endpoints originating from within container infrastructure (Docker network, Kubernetes pod CIDR, or calls to container API gateways). Flag if source is unexpected container or external scanning.

suggestion.title: Malicious LNK File Creation Masquerading Original Documents
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the malware hides the originals and replaces them with malicious shortcuts bearing the same names.' Detection opportunity for document masquerading and file type substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of .LNK files with names matching document extensions (.docx, .xlsx, .pdf, etc.) in user profile directories. Correlate with process execution spawning from shortcut files (cmd.exe, powershell.exe child processes from lnk execution). Baseline document-heavy directories for rapid .LNK file proliferation.

suggestion.title: Tor Executable Process Execution (ugate.exe)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'establishing communications with the command-and-control (C2) host using a Tor executable (ugate.exe).' Direct IOC and execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ugate.exe execution or any Tor executable spawned by unexpected parent processes (esp. from USB-mounted or temp directories). Correlate with localhost:9050 network connections (Tor proxy indicator). Monitor for process names matching common Tor launcher patterns.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Creation Monitoring USB Device Insertion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'The worm creates a scheduled task that monitors for newly connected USB storage devices.' Clear persistence and propagation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled task creation referencing removable drive detection or USB device monitoring. Look for tasks triggering on device arrival with payloads from temp/AppData/USB locations. Correlate with PowerShell/cmd.exe task creation commands executed outside administrative context.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Code Execution via C2 Download (cfile)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the malware downloads JavaScript content into a file named 'cfile,' and executes it on the infected machine.' Remote code execution vector via dynamic JavaScript.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wscript.exe/cscript.exe execution, particularly with file paths containing 'cfile' or temp directory references. Alert on JavaScript execution followed by curl, PowerShell, or cmd.exe child processes. Check for unexpected .js/.jse file creation from network-accessible locations.

suggestion.title: Clipboard Monitoring for Cryptocurrency Wallet Data
suggestion.rationale: Article details repeated clipboard reads 'Every half a second, the malware checks the clipboard for the following data: 12-word BIP39 seed phrases, 24-word BIP39 seed phrases, Ethereum private keys...' Behavioral collection pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes with elevated clipboard access frequencies (polling intervals <1 second). Baseline normal clipboard tools (Office, browsers). Alert on unusual processes reading clipboard in rapid succession. Correlate clipboard reads with network exfiltration or credential access patterns.

suggestion.title: Frequent Screenshot Capture with Curl-Based Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'the malware also captures five screenshots of the victim's screen every ten seconds and sends them to the C2 using the curl tool.' Distinct collection + exfiltration pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on curl.exe execution with Tor-related arguments or localhost:9050 proxy references. Monitor for screenshot-related tool usage (built-in Windows APIs) followed by curl network activity. Baseline curl usage and flag unexpected encryption/proxy parameters. Correlate timing of curl invocations with screenshot intervals.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Suspicious Kernel Driver Load
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'driver-based stealth' as the Windows expansion mechanism—this is the core persistence and evasion vector for kernel-mode backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .sys file loads from non-standard paths, unsigned drivers, or drivers loaded via user-mode processes. Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services for new service entries with ImagePath pointing to suspicious locations or without publisher metadata.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Process or File Hiding
suggestion.rationale: Driver-based stealth implementations hide processes, files, or connections at kernel level. The article's defining characteristic is 'driver-based stealth,' implying kernel-mode filter hooks or callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process or file discrepancies: events in EDR/ETW logs with no corresponding handle in process enumeration, files written but not appearing in filesystem APIs, or registry writes followed by invisible reads. Correlate with unsigned driver loads.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Network Interception Driver
suggestion.rationale: Rootkit backdoors often install NDIS or WFP drivers to intercept traffic, enabling stealthy C2. Article describes 'driver-based stealth' for backdoor functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services for NDIS or WFP entries. Detect kernel-mode driver installations that precede anomalous network flows or encrypted traffic without user-mode applications.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Signed/Vulnerable Driver
suggestion.rationale: Many Windows rootkits bootstrap kernel execution by exploiting publicly known vulnerable drivers (CVE-based). Pipeline should detect this stepping stone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user-mode processes invoking or writing to known exploitable drivers (e.g., Gigabyte APP Center, ASUS drivers listed in LOLDriver). Flag privilege-escalation events immediately preceding driver installation.

suggestion.title: System Service Installation for Driver Persistence
suggestion.rationale: SprySOCKS Windows expansion necessarily involves registry-based driver service setup. This is foundational to any kernel-mode persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services entries with Type=1 (kernel driver) and non-standard Start values. Correlate with DeviceFileEvents showing .sys file creation in %SystemRoot%\System32\drivers or alternative paths.

suggestion.title: Kernel Callback Registration and Hooking
suggestion.rationale: Driver-based stealth relies on kernel callbacks (PsSetLoadImageNotifyRoutine, CmRegisterCallback, etc.). Detection should look for callback registration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for patterns indicative of kernel callback registration: rapid successive DeviceDriverLoad events, drivers with elevated runtime behavior (stalling process enumeration, intercepting file operations), or ETW events showing kernel-mode hooks.

suggestion.rationale: Article directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]' with CVE-2026-20253 substituted. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this explicit guidance.
