suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Splunk audit.log for HTTP requests to /services/server/info, /services/indexes, or other critical endpoints with http_status=200 and auth_token=NONE or Authorization header absent. Correlate with source IP reputation (internal vs external); external IPs should never reach critical endpoints unauthenticated.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`. Pipeline produced no use cases despite this instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-fleet Splunk Enterprise asset inventory against known-vulnerable CVE-2026-20253 versions. Flag any instance with version <patched_version> or lacking vendor security patch dated ≥2026-06-21. Include patch-lag analysis (deployment delay vs. KEV publication).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user' access to 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is explicit initial-access boundary behavior. No detection rule proposed for monitoring unauthorized service access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/TCP traffic to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or service-proxy port) originating from non-administrative network segments or anonymous sources. Flag requests lacking valid Splunk auth headers or API tokens.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files' — this is the exploitation impact, but no file-operation detection proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Splunk Enterprise hosts vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253, flag file creation/truncation in unexpected directories (not /opt/splunk/var/etc, /opt/splunk/etc) or suspicious file names (config files, binaries, log files from unauthenticated processes or service-account activity outside normal bounds).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Process Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation path runs through 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — no detection for process-level anomalies or unexpected spawning of file-operations from that service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar child processes (in Splunk Enterprise context) for unexpected file operations, shell spawning, or network connections. Baseline normal sidecar activity and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Tampering via CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file creation/truncation risk extends to Splunk configuration files (inputs.conf, outputs.conf, etc.), enabling persistence or lateral movement. Article does not call this out but it is a plausible follow-on impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk configuration file writes (inputs.conf, outputs.conf, limits.conf, props.conf) for unexpected modifications originating from service accounts or unauthenticated access patterns. Correlate with PostgreSQL sidecar activity or unauthenticated HTTP traffic.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Connection to Localhost MCP Service Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'trigger arbitrary process execution through AutoGen Studio's MCP WebSocket' via 'missing authentication' — this is the direct execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WebSocket connections from browser/agent processes to 127.0.0.1 on high ephemeral ports that lack authentication headers or tokens. Correlate with process creation events occurring shortly after the WebSocket handshake to detect RCE instantiation.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Process Navigating to Untrusted Webpage Followed by Localhost Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'a single malicious webpage can turn an AI browsing agent into a remote code execution vector' by accessing local services via 'unsafe parameter handling'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when AI agent processes (AutoGen, etc.) make outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to external domains, followed within seconds by connections to 127.0.0.1 or localhost on MCP-related ports (default ~8081). Unsafe parameter handling suggests the external webpage injects localhost-targeting payloads.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Process Execution from Agent Parent Context
suggestion.rationale: Attack achieves 'RCE on the host running your AI agent' — process execution on the underlying machine from the agent's process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual child process creation where the parent is an AI agent process (AutoGen Studio, etc.) and the child is unrelated to expected agent operations (PowerShell, cmd, bash, etc.). Alert on execution in SYSTEM or unexpected privilege contexts, indicating successful privilege escalation from the RCE.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Localhost Trust Boundary by Web Content
suggestion.rationale: Explicit attack vector: 'abusing trust in localhost' — the research shows 'traditional boundaries like localhost are no longer secure' when agents can browse untrusted content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network connections originating from web browser or content-parsing processes (user-agent strings visible in proxy logs) targeting 127.0.0.1, ::1, or localhost hostnames on non-standard or high-number ports. Filter for requests containing parameter values or payloads typical of MCP protocol exploitation.

suggestion.title: AutoGen Studio MCP Service Accepting Unauthenticated Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies AutoGen Studio's MCP WebSocket as the vulnerable service endpoint exploited to achieve RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AutoGen Studio MCP service logs (if available) for WebSocket messages lacking required authentication tokens, originating from unexpected source IPs/ports, or containing serialized command payloads. Cross-reference with network logs showing the originating process is a browser context.

suggestion.title: Malicious Parameter Injection via Webpage into LocalHost Service
suggestion.rationale: Attack leverages 'unsafe parameter handling' in the MCP service — the malicious webpage crafts HTTP/WebSocket requests with injected parameters targeting localhost.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP or WebSocket requests from browser processes targeting localhost services (127.0.0.1, localhost) with URL-encoded or JSON parameters containing shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks), process names, or command keywords. Alert on any successful 200/101 response followed by process creation.

suggestion.title: Vertex AI SDK Unexpected Bucket Upload Redirection
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: SDK hijacked to upload models to attacker-controlled buckets via bucket squatting. Pipeline missed detection of SDK attempting to upload to GCS paths outside expected project hierarchy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GCP Audit Logs for Vertex AI SDK (via user-agent or source identity) initiating gsutil or storage.objects.create calls to bucket names not matching project naming conventions or not in approved bucket list. Flag if bucket name appears to be typosquatting legitimate infrastructure (e.g., similarity to 'vertex-ai-models-*' patterns).

suggestion.title: GCS Bucket Name Similarity to Google Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Bucket squatting attack requires attacker to register buckets with names resembling legitimate Google or project buckets. Article states attackers 'hijack model uploads' via squatting—detect attempts to create/own lookalike buckets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new GCS bucket creation where bucket name contains Levenshtein distance ≤2 from known Google Vertex AI or project bucket prefixes, or uses common typosquatting patterns (e.g., adding/removing underscores, swapping characters). Cross-reference with bucket ownership to detect external account ownership of look-alike buckets.

suggestion.title: SDK Version Downgrade or Dependency Confusion in Vertex AI
suggestion.rationale: Bucket squatting often works via dependency confusion—attacker publishes lower-versioned malicious SDK. Article mentions 'SDK flaw'—detect when teams are coerced to use unexpected SDK versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/poetry/npm install logs for google-cloud-aiplatform or vertex-ai package installs from non-official registries (PyPI index confusion), version downgrades, or pinned-to-patch versions that deviate from team standard. Alert if package hash differs from expected Google-signed version.

suggestion.title: GCS Upload Credentials Exfiltration via Malicious SDK
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked SDK can capture upload credentials. Article attack involves 'model uploads via bucket squatting'—detection should flag credential leakage patterns when SDK interactions occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Vertex AI SDK processes initiating unusual outbound connections to non-Google IPs while GCS credentials are in memory or environment variables. Monitor for unexpected exfiltration of gs:// signed URLs or service account keys in HTTP request bodies to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Model Upload to Out-of-Band GCS Bucket
suggestion.rationale: Core attack step: attackers 'hijack model uploads'. Detection must catch when model training/deployment pipelines write to unexpected buckets instead of project-approved locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Vertex AI training jobs and model uploads for write operations to GCS buckets outside a whitelist of approved buckets per project/service account. Alert on upload_directory or model_artifact paths pointing to buckets with differing project IDs or cross-account ownership.

suggestion.title: Cross-Project GCS Access from Vertex AI Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Bucket squatting attack enables cross-project bucket access if service account permissions are overly broad. Article mentions 'hijack'—detect lateral movement into attacker-controlled GCS resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Vertex AI service accounts (vertex-sa@*, compute-sa@*) attempt storage.objects operations on GCS buckets outside their home project. Combine with unusual caller_ip or caller_principal to identify compromised or hijacked credentials.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure — Splunk Enterprise Inventory by Version
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entry requires immediate patching (due 2026-06-21). Pipeline must establish baseline of exposed Splunk Enterprise instances before hunting exploitation. Template explicitly references asset-exposure hunt as canonical first step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Splunk Enterprise instances in environment by asset inventory, extract product version, cross-reference against CVE-2026-20253 patched versions. Prioritize internet-facing instances. Flag all unpatched instances as critical by 2026-06-21 due date.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated user' can exploit via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline should detect: (1) inbound HTTP/TCP connections to known Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports without valid session auth, (2) 401/403 responses followed by state-changing operations, (3) out-of-band PostgreSQL protocol traffic from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar (typically localhost:5432 or custom port) from non-Splunk-service sources. Baseline expected callers; alert on unauthenticated protocol attempts or missing API authentication headers. Correlate with file I/O spike.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk PostgreSQL Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files through PostgreSQL sidecar.' This is direct impact post-exploitation. Pipeline must detect file operations (writes, deletes, truncates) where parent process is Splunk/PostgreSQL but target paths are outside expected Splunk directories (logs, indexes, metadata).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation operations initiated from Splunk PostgreSQL service account (splunk, postgres, or custom service user) where target path is outside /opt/splunk/*, /var/log/splunk/*, /var/lib/splunk/*. Especially flag system-critical paths: /etc/passwd, /boot/*, /root/*, or executable directories.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Port Scanning or Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article implies PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint is exploitable if accessible. Attackers must first discover or probe the endpoint. Pipeline should detect: port scans targeting expected Splunk sidecar ranges, connection attempts from unusual source ASNs/geolocations, failed authentication attempts followed by successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed connection attempts to Splunk PostgreSQL port (5432 or custom) from single source within short window. Flag especially: external IPs, TOR exit nodes, IPs associated with vulnerability scanning frameworks, or sources with no legitimate Splunk dependency.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Account Privilege Escalation or Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker gains file write via PostgreSQL sidecar, next-stage tactics likely include writing cronjobs, modifying shell startup files, or injecting credentials. Article doesn't describe post-exploitation but pipeline should model likely follow-on attack vectors from persistent file write capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file modifications to Splunk service user's home directory startup files (.bashrc, .bash_profile, cron jobs, etc.) or system-wide persistence mechanisms (systemd timers, init scripts) where writer is the Splunk service account or PostgreSQL process. Alert on unexpected modifications, especially with embedded commands or exfiltration indicators.

suggestion.title: Title/Body CVE Mismatch Alert (Data Quality Issue)
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'CVE-2024-49035 Microsoft Partner Center' but body entirely describes 'CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise.' Pipeline should have flagged this discrepancy as a data integrity failure before processing. This suggests articles are being conflated or ingestion is corrupted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Meta-alert: do NOT trust any other IOCs or MITRE mappings from this article until title/body mismatch is resolved at source. Pipeline must validate CVE in title matches CVE in body before proceeding. Return to original CISA KEV feed to confirm correct CVE ID.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines attack surface as 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' exposed to unauthenticated users. Requires hunting for Splunk instances with accessible sidecar services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for inbound connections to Splunk sidecar ports (typically PostgreSQL-adjacent, port 5432 variants) from external sources with no prior authentication session. Correlate with vulnerability scanner output to identify CVE-2026-20253-affected Splunk builds.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly described as 'missing authentication for critical function.' Detection must capture failed and successful unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints lacking valid authentication credentials, session tokens, or Splunk user context. Baseline legitimate sidecar activity and flag anomalous access patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation and Truncation via Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This file manipulation must be detected across Splunk's critical directories and data stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation and truncation events in Splunk installation directories, index stores, and configuration paths without corresponding authorized process activity. Flag bulk file deletion patterns as data destruction attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Interruption Following File Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Truncating arbitrary Splunk files (indexes, binaries, state files) would trigger service failures. Article phrase 'truncate arbitrary files' indicates data destruction capability targeting operational continuity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected Splunk service restarts, fatal errors in logs, or availability drops with prior suspicious file operations or unauthenticated sidecar access within a 5-minute window. Establish baseline index availability metrics.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Enterprise Admin API
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct initial access without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/GET requests to Splunk admin endpoints (/_internal/, /services/) lacking valid session tokens or authentication headers, originating from non-whitelisted IP ranges. Focus on PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints exposed via HTTP.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the attack permits 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct file-system impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and deletion in Splunk's data directories ($SPLUNK_HOME/var/lib/splunk/*) and PostgreSQL directories for unexpected writes or truncations. Correlate timing with unauthenticated HTTP access patterns. Flag rapid or bulk file modifications indicative of batch attacks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Indicator Matching
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry denotes active exploitation in the wild; federal patch due 2026-06-21 requires urgent asset-exposure baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference scanner output and asset database for Splunk Enterprise versions matching vulnerable ranges. Prioritize internet-facing instances. Validate patch status and access controls. Flag instances without network segmentation or authentication proxies in front.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure — Splunk Enterprise

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances exposed on internet-facing endpoints without authentication controls. Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20253 matches; correlate against asset inventory to identify systems with patch lag or missing updates.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint — Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exists 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exploitation vector but pipeline generated no detection for endpoint access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated or unexpected connections to internal PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically non-standard ports). Flag any connection attempts from external IP ranges or without credential submission preceding database operations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation — Splunk Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is the impact mechanism but no use case captures file operation abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation or truncation operations initiated from unauthenticated network context or from PostgreSQL sidecar process running with unexpected privileges. Flag file operations on sensitive Splunk directories (configs, indexes, logs).

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass — Splunk Critical Function Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly mentions 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function.' Pipeline should detect authentication bypass attempts but generated no such use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise endpoints for requests to critical functions (file operations, configuration changes, data access) arriving without valid session tokens or credentials in Authorization headers. Baseline normal credential submission patterns and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation — Indicator Match
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline IOCs are empty. Article recommends 'CVE match against your vulnerability scanner' — the CVE itself is the primary detection indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest vulnerability scanner results and flag any Splunk Enterprise instances with CVE-2026-20253 present (unpatched or unverified patch status). Correlate against federal due-date (2026-06-21) to identify remediation SLA breaches.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar — Data Truncation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states files can be 'truncated' — this is a specific destructive operation indicating either data exfiltration prep or denial-of-service. No use case for this impact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TRUNCATE or mass DELETE operations against PostgreSQL sidecar service initiated from unauthenticated context. Flag any table truncation within minutes of suspicious endpoint access or authentication bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Apache Spark ACL Bypass and Shell RCE (CVE-2022-33891)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'if an admin had enabled an ACL authentication filter, an attacker could bypass it and execute shell commands as the Spark service user' and notes 'ZeroBot botnet using this vulnerability to exploit and propagate malware through affected systems' in December 2022, with CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities confirmation. Zero UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell command execution spawned by Spark service account (java/spark processes) executing cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or /bin/sh with network-triggered invocation patterns. Detect ACL-bypass indicators such as unauthenticated inbound connections to Spark ports followed by child process execution.

suggestion.title: GitPython Command Injection via Malicious Repository URL (CVE-2022-24439)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'GitPython library did not properly sanitize git commands in versions below 3.1.30' and CTF challenge where 'with some clever syntax tricks, they could execute any arbitrary command.' Explicitly flagged as supply chain risk in CI/CD pipelines. Zero UC generated despite clear exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git clone/pull operations that spawn unexpected child processes (shell interpreters, curl, wget). Detect shell metacharacters in git repository URL parameters (backticks, $(), pipe, semicolon). Flag Python processes executing non-git binaries after git method invocation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Endpoint Access Bypass (Insecure Access Control)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Protecting Camp' challenge where flag was 'tucked away at a hidden endpoint only accessible locally' but exploited via 'unsafe functionality of the app's API and how it retrieved metadata for items on sale.' Paralleled to 'Azure Power Apps misconfiguration exposing over 38 million records.' No detection UC generated for this OWASP Top 10 issue.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls accessing localhost/internal-only endpoints from non-localhost sources. Detect enumeration of metadata endpoints with sequential IDs or path traversal patterns. Flag privilege escalation in API access where a user accesses resources beyond their authorization scope via metadata retrieval tricks.

suggestion.title: ZeroBot Malware Exploitation Campaign (Spark CVE-2022-33891)
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'Microsoft observed the ZeroBot botnet using this vulnerability to exploit and propagate malware through affected systems' in December 2022. Named threat actor with documented active exploitation. No actor-based detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ZeroBot C2 communication patterns or malware signatures associated with Spark exploitation campaigns. Monitor for binary downloads and execution following Spark RCE success. Correlate network traffic to known ZeroBot infrastructure with Spark process creation events.

suggestion.title: GitPython Improper CVE Fix Bypass (CVE-2023-40267)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'CVE-2023-40267 — an improper fix of this bug, which still allowed code execution via crafted repo URLs' indicating second-order vulnerability in GitPython mitigation. Represents supply chain persistence of a known vulnerability class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation using crafted Git repository URLs that bypass CVE-2022-24439 patches. Look for Git operation logs with URL-encoded shell metacharacters, double-encoded payloads, or alternative injection vectors. Detect shell execution following failed git command parsing.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Sidecar Service Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detection requires identifying external/untrusted connections to this endpoint without valid Splunk authentication tokens or session credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk sidecar service endpoints from external/untrusted sources lacking valid Splunk authentication headers (X-Splunk-Authorization, Authorization tokens, or active session cookies). Baseline internal access patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation or Truncation via Splunk Service Processes
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Endpoint-initiated file operations require detection at file-system layer to catch post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, modification, or truncation events initiated by Splunk service processes (splunkd, postgres, sidecar daemons) to unexpected paths outside documented baselines. Flag rapid bulk file operations or writes to system-critical directories.

suggestion.title: Port Enumeration Targeting Splunk Service Ports
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first discover the exposed sidecar service before exploitation. Detection of external port scanning or service probing precedes successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify scanning patterns targeting documented Splunk service ports and sidecar-related ports from external sources. Look for connection attempts without completed handshakes or rapid sequential SYN packets indicating enumeration.

suggestion.title: API Requests to Critical Functions without Authentication Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'missing authentication for critical function.' Detection requires identifying API calls to critical endpoints lacking valid authentication credentials or session state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to Splunk critical-function endpoints (particularly those handling file operations or system modifications) that lack Authorization headers, API tokens, or valid session cookies. Alert on unauthenticated POST/PUT/DELETE operations.

suggestion.title: Temporal Correlation: Unauthenticated Endpoint Access Followed by File Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain: external access to sidecar endpoint → file operations. Correlation of unauthenticated sidecar access with subsequent file creation/truncation events indicates active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate firewall/network logs showing external access to Splunk sidecar endpoint with subsequent file-system events (creation, truncation, deletion) within 60-second window from same source. Flag as exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Asset Inventory

Article references template '../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure' for this hunt. CVE-2026-20253 explicitly named as the matching CVE.

Flag any instance responding to unauthenticated connection attempts to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or non-standard variants managed by Splunk).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthorized File Operation Attempts

Flag discrepancies where scanner reports 'not vulnerable' but product version falls within vulnerable ranges for CVE-2026-20253. suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Service Port Reconnaissance

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connection attempts to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints from external or untrusted networks. Look for incomplete handshakes, multiple failed connection attempts to the same port across multiple source IPs, or known scanner user-agents attempting connection. Baseline expected sidecar traffic and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation (Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline should detect external requests to this endpoint.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/truncation events on Splunk Enterprise systems in sensitive directories (config, data, logs), especially when correlated with unauthenticated API requests to PostgreSQL endpoints or anomalous process behavior.

suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation + T1190 implies active exploitation against externally-exposed assets. Federal due date 2026-06-21 mandates rapid inventory and triage.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for file creation or truncation in Splunk directories (config, data, diag) initiated by PostgreSQL sidecar or Splunk processes without corresponding authenticated user action. Baseline normal sidecar file activity and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Port Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the vulnerability surface; asset-exposure template recommends vulnerability scanning. Probing for exposed sidecar is prerequisite to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline and hunt for inbound network connections to Splunk sidecar service ports from external/unexpected sources. Look for scanning patterns or connection attempts from non-Splunk infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Splunk Log Tampering via Arbitrary File Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Truncation capability described in article could be weaponized to destroy logs or configuration files post-exploitation. 'Truncate arbitrary files' combined with 'critical function' suggests impact scope includes audit/evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mass or sequential file truncation events on Splunk servers, especially in log and config directories. Correlate suspicious truncations with failed authentication attempts or sidecar access logs showing unauthenticated access.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure Hunt (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in template' and states 'it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Asset-exposure hunt is the standard operational response for CISA KEV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Use vulnerability scanner to identify all Splunk Enterprise instances with version numbers vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with network exposure (public-facing, accessible from untrusted networks). Flag patch status vs. federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Detection (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit 'publicly-facing application' — this is asset exposure, the canonical first step. Article explicitly recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline surfaced no detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances accessible from untrusted networks on default or custom HTTP/HTTPS ports. Cross-reference against asset inventory; any exposed instance matching vulnerable versions should trigger immediate escalation given CVE-2026-20253 is actively exploited (CISA KEV status).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline extracted neither endpoint identifier nor exploitation pattern. This is the direct attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar service paths (typically backend/internal service routes). Look for requests from external/untrusted sources or unusual User-Agent/authentication patterns. Unauthenticated exploitation means no login event precedes the malicious request.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is post-exploitation impact. No use case captured the behavioral anomaly of file mutations via sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On vulnerable Splunk instances, monitor for suspicious file creation or truncation events that correlate with sidecar process activity or inbound requests to sidecar endpoints. Baseline normal file operations; alert on writes/deletes to unexpected paths (config, data, binaries).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE explicitly and marks as CISA KEV (active exploitation). Pipeline did not surface CVE as IOC. Minimal detection: confirm patch status across Splunk fleet against CVE-2026-20253.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner or asset-management DB for Splunk Enterprise instances and filter by version/patch status against CVE-2026-20253 advisory. Flag any unpatched or patched-but-not-verified instances for immediate review given federal patch due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Sidecar Service Anomalous Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article does not explicitly detail the sidecar endpoint path, but 'PostgreSQL sidecar service' is the attack surface. Detect lateral abuse of sidecar after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated or automated requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints from compromised internal hosts or from external sources with successful responses. Compare against baseline; exploit attempts often probe multiple endpoints in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates checking 'your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-20253 and warns that 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline did not generate the canonical asset-exposure hunt referenced in the article template guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Splunk Enterprise instances report vulnerability or patch status matching CVE-2026-20253, even if previously marked patched. Create audit trigger for instances still vulnerable as of the federal due date (2026-06-21). CISA KEV presence implies active wild exploitation—prior compliance assertions may be stale.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'unauthenticated user' accessing 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline produced no network or service-level detection for this specific abuse path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar service (internal endpoint) from unexpected sources or without valid authentication credentials. Monitor for HTTP requests without auth tokens to sidecar administrative endpoints. Establish baseline of legitimate internal-only connectivity patterns.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation and Truncation on Splunk Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files.' Pipeline missed the endpoint-level impact detection for file-system abuse from the compromised service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file-creation or truncation operations executed under Splunk service accounts or the PostgreSQL sidecar process. Flag mass file deletions, zero-byte overwrites, or suspicious writes to Splunk config/data/log directories. Correlate with failed-authentication or sidecar-access logs to confirm exploitation.

suggestion.title: Missing-Authentication Endpoint Exploitation on Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'missing authentication for critical function.' Pipeline did not generate detection for authentication-bypass or no-auth endpoint exploitation patterns against Splunk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful requests to Splunk critical or admin endpoints that lack valid authentication tokens, session cookies, or API credentials. Monitor Splunk's _internal logs for auth-bypass indicators. Combine with network alerts on sidecar-endpoint access to confirm CVE exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Destruction Indicators on Splunk Assets
suggestion.rationale: Attack end-state is 'truncate arbitrary files'—classic destructive impact. Pipeline ignored the impact-phase hunt for signs of data wiping or config/log destruction on compromised systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid or suspicious mass file deletion, truncation, or zero-out operations targeting Splunk configuration, backup, or log stores. Cross-check timestamps with sidecar-access anomalies. Data destruction via file-manipulation is often a precursor to exfiltration, ransomware, or anti-forensics campaigns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/REST requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints (e.g., /services/postgres*, /admin/postgres*) without valid Authorization headers or session tokens. Look for requests that succeed despite 401/403 responses to similar endpoints from the same source. Baseline legitimate sidecar traffic by source IP and endpoint. CISA KEV: exploitation in the wild.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation or Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'could allow...create or truncate arbitrary files.' Direct impact—this is what defenders need to hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor the PostgreSQL sidecar process for file system modifications (creation, deletion, truncation) in sensitive paths (Splunk config, app directories, log aggregation paths). Correlate file-system events with HTTP access logs; alert on file operations preceded by unauthenticated sidecar endpoint requests within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-20253 and sets federal patch due date 2026-06-21. Standard asset-exposure hunt—pipeline must extract CVE and drive scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances. Flag unpatched versions (pre-2026-06-21 releases vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253). Prioritize public-facing instances. Cross-reference with network-reachability scans. CISA KEV entry guarantees active exploitation.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Port Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'unauthenticated' access to sidecar 'endpoint'—implies exposed network service. Article does not specify port but PostgreSQL sidecar likely listens on standard (5432) or Splunk-proprietary port.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Splunk Enterprise instances for exposed PostgreSQL sidecar ports (default 5432, or vendor-defined sidecar port). Alert on instances with direct inbound access from untrusted networks. Verify sidecar listening with no authentication wrapper (e.g., reverse-proxy auth or VPN gating absent).

suggestion.title: AI Agent Process Accessing External Malicious Webpage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'a single malicious webpage can turn an AI browsing agent into a remote code execution vector' — must detect when AutoGen, browser agents, or LLM-controlled processes fetch untrusted external content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when AutoGen, agent-runner, or browser-process parents make HTTP/HTTPS GET/POST requests to external domains with low domain-age or no security reputation. Combine with subsequent WebSocket activity to localhost on non-standard ports (esp. 6789) as multi-stage trigger.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WebSocket Connection to Localhost from Agent Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger arbitrary process execution through AutoGen Studio's MCP WebSocket' — RCE occurs via MCP protocol abuse on localhost. Must detect agent-initiated WebSocket to local services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WebSocket connections (TCP/443, 6789, or uncommon ports) from AutoGen or agent processes to 127.0.0.1/::1, especially if unauthenticated or preceded by external webpage fetch. Inspect frame payloads for MCP method calls and command-like strings.

suggestion.title: Unsafe Parameter Injection in MCP Service Call
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unsafe parameter handling' as the exploitation primitive. MCP endpoint does not validate/sanitize parameters, enabling injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect MCP WebSocket frames for payloads containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $, backticks, `cat`, `exec`, etc.), environment variable syntax (${VAR}, %VAR%), or path traversal sequences ('../'). Cross-reference with DeviceProcessEvents to confirm execution occurred.

suggestion.title: Process Execution Spawned from AutoGen/Agent Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary process execution' on the host. RCE manifests as unexpected child processes created by AutoGen or MCP broker services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes of AutoGen, Agent Studio broker, or MCP listener spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or curl/wget with suspicious arguments. Baseline normal operations (legitimate agent tasks) to reduce FP. Alert on parent process that normally spawns no children.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Localhost MCP Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'missing authentication' as a root cause. Local MCP services lack auth gates, allowing any localhost process (including compromised agent) to invoke methods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for MCP service authentication patterns. Detect connections that skip expected credential handshake or use default/empty credentials. Correlate process origin (agent vs. expected admin tools) to flag anomalies; agent processes reaching MCP without auth is high-risk.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Agent-Spawned Process
suggestion.rationale: AutoJack executes code on 'the host running your AI agent.' If agent runs as unprivileged user but spawned processes run as SYSTEM/root, detect the boundary crossing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate parent process (AutoGen, agent service) UID/GID with child process UID/GID. Alert on non-admin parent spawning SYSTEM/root children, especially via indirect mechanisms (COM objects, MCP method invocation). Sequence with prior WebSocket and parameter-injection signals.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Execution via Browser
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Fake Update Lures' in title; classic ClickFix vector of impersonating legitimate update prompts to trigger malware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for browser processes spawning executable installers from temp directories or mismatched signature paths. Alert on child processes of updater-named executables that contact suspicious domains or write to Startup folders.

suggestion.title: New Malware Loader Staging and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'New Loaders'—likely second-stage payloads. Need detection for loader persistence, C2 beaconing, and staging infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous outbound traffic from processes with update-related names to non-Microsoft IPs. Alert on repeated HTTPS beacons with low payload variance or DNS queries for freshly registered domains.

suggestion.title: Startup Persistence via ClickFix Malware
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix historically writes registry keys (HKLM\Run, etc.) to persist. Article mentions malware delivery expansion, implying persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned executables added to Run/RunOnce keys or Startup folders immediately following browser-spawned child processes. Correlate with recent temp file creation.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV 'only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' with federal patch due date 2026-06-21. Directly templatable using provided asset-exposure hunt reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Splunk Enterprise instances against CVE-2026-20253 patch status. Flag any unpatched or missing-patch-date hosts; correlate against remediation deadline for compliance tracking.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'missing authentication for critical function vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated user'. This is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Splunk API endpoints lacking authentication tokens/headers that succeed or receive late-stage rejection (not early 401). Baseline normal auth patterns per endpoint.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Unauthenticated Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation mechanism: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. Monitor for abuse of this interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated or poorly-authenticated connections to PostgreSQL sidecar ports. Track sidecar SQL operations that issue file-manipulation commands; baseline against legitimate Splunk daemon activity.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation by Splunk Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'. Successful exploitation manifests as unexpected file system modifications by Splunk service accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk daemon processes (splunkd, postgres sidecar) creating, truncating, or deleting files outside expected application directories. Flag changes to /etc, system logs, or config paths.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Public Asset Inventory Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and notes CISA KEV tracks exploited vulnerabilities in the wild. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset management tools for Splunk Enterprise instances with CVE-2026-20253 signature match or version ≤ patched baseline. Cross-reference external-facing hosts (internet-routable IPs, public DNS) to identify exposure. Correlate with proxy logs for inbound access attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation vector as 'unauthenticated user' accessing 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. This explicit technique should drive endpoint-network detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk hosts for inbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to PostgreSQL sidecar service ports lacking valid authentication headers or session tokens. Baseline expected internal callers. Alert on external-origin or public-IP source requests.

suggestion.title: File Truncation/Creation via Compromised Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — this is the post-exploitation payload and requires host-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated PostgreSQL sidecar access attempts (network baseline) with subsequent file creation or truncation on the same host within 60 seconds. Flag unexpected modifications to system files, config, or application binaries.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the primary attack vector that must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (patterns like `/postgresql/*`, `/sidecar/*`) that either lack authentication headers entirely or use empty/missing credentials. Prioritize external source IPs. Monitor failed login attempts followed by successful unauthenticated access.

suggestion.title: File Creation/Truncation via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the exploit capability is to 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—need detection for these operations originating from the sidecar process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CREATE TABLE/TRUNCATE/DELETE operations executed through the PostgreSQL sidecar against non-standard tables or against system-critical targets (logs, config files). Flag large batch file deletions or truncations originating from the sidecar service principal.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of CVE-2026-20253 in Splunk (CISA KEV Active)
suggestion.rationale: Entry is in CISA KEV catalog ('observed exploited in the wild')—should hunt for known exploitation signatures and anomalous patterns consistent with active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the legitimate request patterns to Splunk sidecar endpoints (method, payload size, source IP ranges). Alert on deviations: unusual HTTP methods (PUT/DELETE to normally read-only paths), large payloads, requests from non-Splunk-infrastructure IPs, rapid-fire requests in short windows.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the attack path flows through 'a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—need baseline for normal sidecar communication to detect lateral exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to the PostgreSQL sidecar service from unexpected sources (non-Splunk-internal clients, external IPs). Track changes to sidecar service account permissions or process arguments. Alert on sidecar processes spawning child processes or making network connections outside the expected Splunk infrastructure communication pattern.

suggestion.title: Apache Spark ACL Bypass & RCE (CVE-2022-33891) Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation: 'attackers could bypass it and execute shell commands as the Spark service user.' CISA KEV listed; ZeroBot actively exploited in December 2022.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation attempts against Apache Spark ACL authentication. Monitor for shell command execution spawning from Spark service accounts with unusual parent processes, malformed or unauthenticated requests to Spark endpoints, and process accounting showing interactive shells under service accounts.

suggestion.title: GitPython Command Injection RCE (CVE-2022-24439 / CVE-2023-40267)
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates: 'with some clever syntax tricks, they could execute any arbitrary command' via Git command injection. CVE-2023-40267 noted as improper fix, indicating ongoing vulnerability window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect command injection attempts in GitPython operations. Look for git commands embedded with shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, backticks), unusual processes spawned from git/CI-CD contexts, or repo URLs containing embedded shell commands targeting pipeline automation.

suggestion.title: OWASP Broken Access Control - Hidden Endpoint Metadata Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Protecting Camp scenario: players 'could access what they were never supposed to' by 'leveraging unsafe functionality of the app's API.' Mirrors Azure Power Apps misconfiguration exposing 38M records in Sept 2023.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access control bypass attempts via API enumeration. Monitor for non-privileged user accounts accessing admin/hidden endpoints, repeated 404→200 sequences indicating endpoint discovery, metadata retrieval requests outside authenticated scope, and unusual API parameter fuzzing patterns.

suggestion.title: ZeroBot Botnet Spark Exploitation Campaign Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies threat actor: 'ZeroBot botnet using this vulnerability to exploit and propagate malware through affected systems' in December 2022. Real-world active exploitation context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ZeroBot C2 communications and lateral propagation patterns. Monitor for botnet beaconing behavior from compromised Spark services, outbound connections to known ZeroBot C2 infrastructure, malware propagation attempts to adjacent systems, and suspicious Java/Spark process network behavior.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain RCE via CI/CD Pipeline Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes GitPython 'is used in many CI/CD pipelines.' Framing exploitation as supply-chain attack vector affecting downstream targets, not just direct application compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect supply-chain compromise via GitPython or Spark exploitation in CI/CD contexts. Monitor for compromised build artifacts, malicious commits injected post-clone, pipeline execution with elevated privileges post-exploitation, and unexpected artifact mutations or binary modifications during build stages.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user' access 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — implies network exposure. Pipeline missed network-surface detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances with PostgreSQL sidecar port open to untrusted networks (typically port 5432 or variant). Correlate with CVE-2026-20253 scanner results to identify exploitable assets. Look for connection attempts from external IP ranges to Splunk hosts.

suggestion.title: File Create/Truncate via Splunk Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow...to create or truncate arbitrary files' — this is the impact mechanism. Pipeline generated no file-operation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or truncation events originating from Splunk Enterprise process or PostgreSQL sidecar child process. Establish baseline of legitimate Splunk file operations; alert on deviations, especially to system directories or configuration paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article body explicitly references CVE-2026-20253 and CISA KEV status implies active exploitation. Pipeline IOCs were empty; should include baseline asset-inventory correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results identifying Splunk Enterprise versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253 (pre-remediation versions) against network access logs to those hosts. Prioritize instances on Federal networks given CISA KEV and 2026-06-21 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempt to Splunk Critical Function
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function' — absence of auth check is the enabling mechanism. Pipeline should capture log patterns indicating unauthenticated access to normally-protected endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Splunk audit logs, look for unauthenticated requests (empty username field, session=none, or HTTP 401→success sequences) targeting file-write endpoints or administrative functions. In PostgreSQL sidecar logs, detect connections without authentication credentials.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Splunk File Operations Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker has file-manipulation capability via the sidecar, they may attempt to exfiltrate, corrupt, or destroy config/data files. Article's 'create or truncate arbitrary files' directly enables post-exploitation behavior not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid or bulk file creation/truncation in Splunk directories ($SPLUNK_HOME, /opt/splunk). Alert on writes to config files (inputs.conf, props.conf, transforms.conf) or deletion of index data outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Splunk Version Inventory Mismatch with KEV Remediation
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due 2026-06-21; enterprise SOCs must verify inventory. Pipeline ignored the temporal urgency and did not generate inventory or patch-gap hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Splunk Enterprise instances via version API or config endpoint. Flag any version pre-patch for CVE-2026-20253 that is still running post-due-date (2026-06-21). Correlate against patch-management logs to identify lag or missed deployments.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows unauthenticated access through 'a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero asset-exposure detections despite template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances with internet-accessible PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (default port 5432). Alert on inbound traffic to sidecar from untrusted CIDR ranges. Cross-reference against Splunk instances not patched before federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Core attack step: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline completely missed file-operation indicators despite explicit impact description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file truncation operations on Splunk hosts originating from or correlated with PostgreSQL service processes. Alert on rapid file I/O to critical config, state, or log files that do not match normal Splunk maintenance windows. Baseline normal Splunk file-write patterns to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Critical Function Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability categorized as 'missing authentication for critical function'—pipeline mapped T1190 but generated zero authentication-bypass detection use cases despite this being the enabling factor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated or anonymous requests to Splunk critical service endpoints (e.g., file-management APIs, sidecar service handlers). Flag anomalous POST/PUT requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints from external networks. Correlate with failed authentication logs and CVE-2026-20253 scanner results.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Post-Exploitation File Integrity Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV is 'actively being exploited'—pipeline produced no hunt for post-exploitation file artifacts, log deletion, or config tampering indicators that would follow successful file truncation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious gaps or resets in Splunk audit logs, especially around PostgreSQL service restarts. Alert on truncation of audit logs, configuration backups, or state files post-compromision. Track file modification times for known critical Splunk configuration locations.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Splunk Enterprise Internet-Accessible Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited… it's worth one quick check across your fleet.' Prerequisite for T1190 exploitation is an exposed service; detection starts with inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8000, 8089, 8191) with internet-routable IPs. Cross-reference against ownership records and compare to asset inventory to surface unauthorized or forgotten instances. Alert on any public-cloud Splunk deployments without explicit WAF/IP-restriction controls.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the direct exploitation vector; must detect requests lacking auth tokens to sidecar paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk access logs for POST/PUT/GET requests to sidecar service endpoints (e.g., paths containing 'sidecar', 'postgres', or known endpoint URIs) where Authorization header is absent, empty, or invalid. Baseline on your environment first; look for unauthenticated requests that would normally require auth.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files' is the stated impact. Detect the file operations themselves at the OS or Splunk logging layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events in Splunk directories (e.g., /opt/splunk, $SPLUNK_HOME) where the parent process is PostgreSQL, splunkd, or unidentified service processes. Look for suspicious bulk deletes or rewrites of logs, configs, or indexes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Positive — Splunk Enterprise Missing Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Standard patch-lag detection: scanners may mark vulnerable but unpatched systems; this should trigger mandatory remediation workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest vulnerability scan results (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) and alert or escalate any host detected with CVE-2026-20253 in Splunk Enterprise. Flag if detected but not yet remediated 7 days after federal due date (2026-06-21 + 7 days = 2026-06-28); escalate per compliance SLA.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Service Endpoint Access from External/Untrusted IP
suggestion.rationale: Article: Missing auth vulnerability is on 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint,' implying a network-accessible service. Detect access from unexpected network sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP(S) requests to sidecar endpoints from IPs outside your corporate network, cloud VPN ranges, or trusted partner ranges. Baseline your environment first; any external access to these internal-only endpoints is suspicious.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — the initial exploitation vector must generate detectable authentication failures or anomalous endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints that fail authentication or bypass credentials. Flag anomalous access patterns to API endpoints that would normally require session tokens or service-to-service authentication.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary File Truncation via CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact as 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — file manipulation events correlated with unauthenticated endpoint access are the exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file creation/truncation events with HTTP access logs from Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar. Alert on files reduced to zero-length or deleted without matching administrative action in change management systems.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-20253 Scanner Probes and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation — scanning precedes weaponization. Detect early-stage probes to vulnerable PostgreSQL endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated or sequential HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar API paths from external sources, particularly to error pages or non-standard routes that reveal service presence and version information.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Exploitation Persistence via Arbitrary File Write
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'create or truncate arbitrary files' capability enables backdoor placement and persistence mechanisms after initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of executable or script files in system directories (e.g., /bin, /etc, Windows\System32) originating from Splunk or its PostgreSQL sidecar process, lacking corresponding administrative authorization.

suggestion.title: Detect Forensic Log Destruction via File Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file truncation capability extends to audit logs — attackers will destroy evidence. Article describes precise capability to 'truncate arbitrary files' including logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden zero-sizing or truncation of security event logs, application logs, or audit trails. Flag any log file truncation sourced from Splunk or PostgreSQL sidecar processes outside scheduled maintenance.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and cites federal due-date 2026-06-21 — asset inventory correlation against vulnerability scanners is operationally mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all Splunk Enterprise instances in asset inventory against CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability scan results. Prioritize any vulnerable instance with network exposure or public-facing configuration. Confirm patch status via process/software version inspection.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match — CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise
