suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise installations vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Alert on any instances not patched by federal due date 2026-06-21. Correlate version data with vulnerability database.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes KEV entries target 'exposed assets' and unauthenticated exploit requires network accessibility. Asset-exposure template referenced but no UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise ports (8089, 8000, sidecar service ports) directly accessible from untrusted external networks. Cross-reference with asset inventory to find internet-exposed vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'unauthenticated user...through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This service-level access pattern is the actual exploitation channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints without valid Splunk authentication. Alert on POST/PUT operations from external IPs or untrusted network ranges to sidecar ports.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation outcome as 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Pipeline missed the behavioral detection for actual impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Splunk Enterprise hosts, alert on file write/truncate operations initiated by PostgreSQL sidecar process or originating from sidecar service ports, especially in system-critical directories. Correlate with unauthenticated external network access.

suggestion.title: Malicious Supply-Chain Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'thousands of organizations' were impacted over 3 years by importing the backdoored `github.com/botdb-go/bolt` v1.3.1. No detection use case for alerting on installation of known-malicious package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Go dependency resolution or package manager logs show installation of `github.com/botdb-go/bolt` any version, or legitimate `github.com/boltdb/bolt` v1.3.1 specifically. Cross-reference against Go vulnerability database GO-2025-3451 for version pinning.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatting Package Registry Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'malicious Go Module Mirror was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' No detection for suspicious package names resembling legitimate ones in supply-chain context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag requests to package registries (Go Module Proxy, npm, PyPI) for package names with Levenshtein distance < 2 from known-legitimate packages, or DNS queries to lookalike domains of package registry mirrors.

suggestion.title: Module Cache Reversion Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' even after reversion. Detect when a package version is removed from source but continues being served from cache/mirror.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go Module Proxy / package registry responses for version timestamps: alert if client requests a version with creation date before removal date, or if HTTP headers indicate stale cache serving for revoked packages.

suggestion.title: Remote Command & Control from Backdoored Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states backdoor 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands.' No C2 detection for traffic initiated by compromised Go package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For known-infected binaries compiled with botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1, hunt outbound C2 traffic via DNS beaconing or HTTP POST to attacker infrastructure. Correlate process creation of Go binaries with unusual external connections within 60s of import.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Integrity: Dependency Hash Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 3-year persistence due to module caching. Detect when cached/installed package hash diverges from package registry authoritative source or Snyk/Go vuln database checksums.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On build/deployment: compute SHA256 of installed Go modules, compare against checksums in go.sum or official Snyk advisory SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMBOLTDBGOBOLT-868841. Alert on mismatch or missing checksums.

suggestion.title: Deprecated/Revoked Package Still in Production Dependency Tree
suggestion.rationale: Article: module 'reverted to actual legitimate version however...Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching' resulted in stale backdoor remaining 3 years undetected. Detection for when go.mod or dependency manifests pin revoked/cves packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan go.mod, go.sum, and active process listings for botdb-go/bolt any version, or boltdb/bolt v1.3.1. Cross-reference against Go vulnerability database (GO-2025-3451) and Snyk advisories; alert if found in prod deployments after Feb 7, 2025 removal date.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states 'the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`](../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure)'. This is the primary detection use case and was completely omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on exposed Splunk Enterprise instances matching CVE-2026-20253 surface area. Search for inbound network traffic to PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints (typically internal-only) from external or unusual sources. Prioritize assets where patch deployments lag the 2026-06-21 federal due date.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—direct quote identifying the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connection attempts to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints without valid authentication credentials. Look for successful unauthenticated sessions, connection spike patterns, or probing of internal service ports from external sources or privileged users.

suggestion.title: Splunk System Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploit behavior: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this is the impact mechanism and should have a direct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk system processes (splunkd, PostgreSQL service) for unusual file creation, deletion, or truncation operations outside expected deployment/upgrade windows. Flag unexpected writes to system configuration or data directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry with active exploitation in the wild. Pipeline should detect when vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, OpenVAS) identify this CVE in asset inventories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results that flag CVE-2026-20253 on any Splunk Enterprise instance. Correlate with patch deployment timelines; prioritize assets still vulnerable past 2026-06-21 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Patch Deployment Lag
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal due date and 'patch lag is the silent killer'—yet no detection for identifying systems that have not applied the remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate patch deployment logs with asset inventory post-2026-06-21. Flag any Splunk Enterprise instances where build version or patch level does not match the fixed release. Cross-reference with exposure scope (publicly accessible instances receive higher severity).

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — the endpoint exposure and unauthenticated access are the direct attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk access logs and HTTP proxies for requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (commonly /api/internal/psql or similar) lacking valid authentication tokens. Alert on HTTP 200/201 responses to file-creation endpoints from external IPs without prior successful Splunk authentication.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'could allow... create or truncate arbitrary files' — this is the impact payload that distinguishes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation and truncation events initiated by Splunk service processes (splunkd, python) to unexpected directories (outside /opt/splunk, /var/log, standard app paths). Cross-correlate with preceding PostgreSQL endpoint access logs to establish causal chain.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Instance Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: T1190 classification in the article requires public-facing exposure; CISA KEV format confirms active wild exploitation. Asset inventory must surface externally accessible Splunk instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query cloud asset inventory and firewall NAT/port-forwarding rules to identify Splunk management ports (8089 default) or web UI ports (8000 default) reachable from untrusted networks. Alert on any Splunk instance with internet-routable address lacking compensating network segmentation.

suggestion.title: Failed Splunk Authentication Followed by Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function' — detection should chain failed login attempts to subsequent unauthenticated sidecar requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Splunk authentication failure events (auth_failure, invalid_user) within a 5-minute window with subsequent HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints from the same source IP. Single-attempt bypass attempts (no brute-force) are typical for public-facing exploits.

suggestion.title: Splunk Web/API Access from Non-Standard Ports or Suspicious Paths
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV articles targeting public-facing apps often involve direct endpoint exploitation. Article references 'critical function' endpoint — attackers may access via non-standard URIs or HTTP methods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/PUT requests to /api/internal/* or /__internal/* endpoints lacking authentication headers or valid session tokens. Flag unusual HTTP methods (e.g., OPTIONS, TRACE) or Content-Type mismatches on internal APIs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Internet Exposure (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' exploitation of public-facing assets. CISA KEV requires patch-state validation across fleet. No asset-exposure hunt generated despite being the canonical first hunt for any KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8089, 9997, 8000) reachable from untrusted networks and cross-reference against CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability scanner results. Asset-exposure combined with patch-state validates exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as attack vector for 'unauthenticated user' to perform file operations. No detection for this endpoint or authentication bypass was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports/endpoints lacking valid Splunk authentication tokens. Alert on successful (non-401/403) responses to file-manipulation API calls from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files' as the exploitation outcome. No impact-phase detection for file manipulation from Splunk processes was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation operations from Splunk service accounts (splunkd, postgres sidecar) to unexpected paths (config directories, system logs, audit trails). Baseline expected file I/O and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Log Truncation (Defense Evasion)
suggestion.rationale: File truncation capability ('truncate arbitrary files') can target audit/security logs for covering tracks. No detection for this common post-exploitation technique was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After confirming exploitation risk, monitor for truncation of Splunk internal logs, syslog, or host audit logs originating from compromised Splunk contexts. Truncation of 0-byte files is particularly suspicious.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Payloads Targeting CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active exploitation in the wild. No detection for pre-patch exploitation attempts (web scanner payloads, command injection attempts) was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests containing file-operation payloads (path traversal, shell metacharacters) targeting sidecar endpoints before patches were deployed. Correlate with any IDS/IPS CVE-2026-20253 signatures.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated Access to File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files'. Core attack vector must be detected at initial access point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise web/API endpoints for successful file operation requests (POST/PUT/DELETE to write paths) lacking valid authentication tokens. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses to critical API endpoints to detect exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Anomalous File Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation occurs 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. Need detection for unauthorized file write/delete operations via this service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, deletion, or truncation operations initiated by Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar process. Establish baseline of expected file paths and alert on any filesystem modifications outside standard Splunk maintenance activities.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerable Asset Exposure Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' with Federal due-date 2026-06-21. Need systematic vulnerability exposure assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Splunk Enterprise instances matching CVE-2026-20253 signature. Cross-reference with network exposure maps to identify instances with accessible web ports (8000, 8089) visible to untrusted networks. Escalate any unpatched systems post-deadline.

suggestion.title: Anomalous PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as exploitation vector. Need to detect unauthorized connections to internal service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar port (typically 5432 or custom port) from non-Splunk processes or external sources. Alert on any connections originating from Splunk web session context rather than internal service-to-service communication.

suggestion.title: Splunk Audit and Configuration File Integrity Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Ability to 'truncate arbitrary files' enables audit log deletion and config tampering. Must detect tampering of security-critical files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk critical directories (/opt/splunk/etc, /opt/splunk/var) for unexpected truncation or deletion of configuration, authentication, or audit log files. Alert on any filesystem modifications that could enable persistence or destroy audit trails.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Service Port Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates public-facing vulnerability in network service. Need detection for reconnaissance activity targeting Splunk endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for port scanning or service enumeration activity targeting Splunk web UI ports (8000, 8089) and PostgreSQL sidecar port (5432). Alert on failed connection attempts followed by successful exploitation patterns or tool-like scanning behavior.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Core exploitation vector with zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to PostgreSQL sidecar ports (5432 or service-specific variants) on Splunk Enterprise instances from external sources. Flag connections followed by administrative operations absent corresponding authentication logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Truncation by Splunk Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' No detection mapped to file manipulation despite this being primary destructive action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk daemon processes (splunkd, sidecar) creating or truncating files outside expected Splunk directories or system critical paths. Baseline normal operations; flag anomalies in rapid succession or triggered from network context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scan and Asset Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline omitted simplest indicator: CVE-2026-20253 itself. No vulnerability detection or asset-based UC generated despite CISA KEV status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset management for CVE-2026-20253 on Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference patch management for unpatched systems. Federal due-date 2026-06-21—escalate post-date matches.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Anomalies and Restart Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies sidecar endpoint as attack surface; pipeline missed monitoring service configuration, restart patterns, and authentication state changes within sidecar itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected sidecar service restarts, configuration modifications, disabled authentication checks, or error messages indicating authentication bypass. Correlate process events with Splunk internal logs for anomalous service behavior.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Port Reconnaissance and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes public-facing sidecar endpoint; pipeline missed discovery-phase detection for port scanning or service enumeration attempts against sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or service enumeration targeting PostgreSQL ports (5432) or Splunk sidecar ports on internet-facing instances. Correlate scanner activity with subsequent exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: File Integrity Monitoring for Splunk Critical Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article's primary impact is file creation/truncation; pipeline missed detective control for unauthorized modifications to Splunk configuration and data directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy FIM on /opt/splunk, /etc/splunk, and index directories. Alert on unexpected file creation, deletion, or modification outside maintenance windows, especially bulk operations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Enterprise File Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Zero detection hypothesis offered despite clear behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise instances for POST/PUT requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or internal service ports) originating from unauthenticated sessions. Alert on successful file creation or truncation operations in Splunk directories following exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Public Exposure — Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references template hunt for asset exposure: 'the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`' with explicit instruction to hunt for CVE-2026-20253 across fleet. Pipeline emitted no hunt logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory exposed Splunk Enterprise instances via vulnerability scanner, certificate transparency logs, and shodan queries for 'Splunk' on ports 8000, 8089, 8191. suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Unauthorized Access

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database connections to Splunk internal PostgreSQL sidecar (internal service port) from unauthenticated contexts or external subnets. Alert on any CREATE/TRUNCATE commands initiated via unauthenticated HTTP→database bridge.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write to Splunk Configuration or Data Directories

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Authentication Bypass Attempts — HTTP Anomaly

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar - Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — the service-level endpoint attack surface is the primary exploitation vector and should drive detection logic.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise - Unauthorized File Creation or Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability directly enables 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — file manipulation is the concrete impact indicator of successful exploitation that should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation or truncation operations from or coinciding with PostgreSQL sidecar process activity. Baseline normal file operations in critical directories and flag anomalous patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise - Vulnerability Scan and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-20253 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' — pipeline generated no detection logic for the primary IOC or compliance hunt.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation or Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'create or truncate arbitrary files' as the exploitation outcome. File-level indicators are the direct manifestation of this impact phase.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Unpatched Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires federal patch by 2026-06-21. Article specifies 'Splunk Enterprise' with no version constraint; all unpatched versions are exploitable. Asset-exposure hunt is canonical for KEV entries.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Health Degradation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Malicious file creation/truncation via the sidecar would likely cause process crashes, restarts, or error spikes. This is a behavioral indicator of active exploitation.

Correlate unexpected restarts with file I/O anomalies and unauthenticated connection attempts within a 5-minute window. Alert on multiple restarts within 1 hour.

Alert on new files appearing in bin/ or scripts/ directories without change management tickets.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`.' Pipeline must generate vulnerability scanner detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanner probes (Nessus, Qualys, Shodan) fingerprinting Splunk Enterprise for CVE-2026-20253 exploitability. Monitor for version-enumeration API calls and unauthenticated endpoint probing patterns characteristic of active exploitation scanning.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector stated: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Requires detection of endpoint access without valid authentication.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access Attempt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk HTTP access logs for requests to sidecar endpoints without valid authentication tokens or session IDs. Baseline known administrative IPs and alert on external sources or failed-then-successful patterns (brute-force recovery).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP 200 response from rclone RC API endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated GET and HEAD requests' trigger RCE—network detections should flag successful unauthenticated RC API access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to rclone RC listening ports (default 5572, but configurable via --rc-addr) returning HTTP 200/204 responses where requests originate from non-localhost sources and lack Authorization headers or valid session tokens. Compare against whitelist of known authorized RC API consumers. Low-volume baseline of unauthenticated RC hits indicates reconnaissance or exploitation.

suggestion.title: Rclone RC API request payload with command-execution backend options
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'backend options that execute local commands during initialization'—missing payload-level detection for request bodies containing command-injection options (exec, script, system).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse HTTP request bodies/query parameters sent to rclone RC API endpoints; alert on inline remote instantiation syntax containing command-execution keywords (exec, script, system, shell, bash, powershell, cmd, python, etc.) or shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, ||, $(), backticks). Correlate with Processes.parent_process=rclone for execution confirmation.

suggestion.title: Rclone process launched without authentication when --rc-serve is present
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the vulnerability requires --rc-serve without auth flags—detecting NEW process launches (not just inventory) with this risky configuration provides early warning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation of rclone binary where ProcessCommandLine contains --rc-serve AND does NOT contain any of: --rc-user, --rc-pass, --rc-htpasswd. Establish baseline of legitimate unauthenticated RC deployments (CI/CD, admin tools) and whitelist to reduce FP. Tuning: flag first occurrence and track persistence.

suggestion.title: Rclone RC API file/config mutation without prior authentication
suggestion.rationale: Attack exploits inline remote instantiation 'during initialization'—detecting config mutations (POST/PUT to /config, /remote endpoints) without prior auth token indicates exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT/PATCH requests to rclone RC API /config, /remote, or /options endpoints that lack Authorization headers or valid auth tokens. Track baseline of legitimate config mutations. Alert on mutations from unexpected sources. Correlate with command-execution options in request payload.

suggestion.title: Rclone process version check: detect old versions that shipped with CVE-2026-41179 unfixed
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'bypassing CVE-2026-41179 fix'—detecting deployments of rclone versions that shipped with the predecessor vulnerability unfixed provides continuous compliance beyond just this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract rclone version from process command-line or binary metadata; flag versions known to ship with CVE-2026-41179 unfixed (versions prior to known fix release). Maintain dynamic blocklist of versions with known RCE vectors. Alert on first process launch; track over time for persistent deployment.

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Internet Exposure (CVE-2026-20253 Prerequisite)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability is exploitable only on 'public-facing' instances per T1190 context. Asset exposure is the prerequisite for exploitation detection and remediation tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances listening on internet-accessible ports (8089, 8000). Query external asset discovery and compare against internal vulnerability scanning to surface unmanaged or unpatched instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This authentication bypass is the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk HTTP logs for requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints that return successful status codes (200/201) without valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Flag POST/PUT/DELETE requests from external or unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: File Creation or Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' File manipulation payload is detectable through file system auditing and correlated with endpoint access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful unauthenticated sidecar endpoint requests with subsequent file creation, modification, or deletion events. Look for suspicious writes to critical Splunk directories ($SPLUNK_HOME/etc, bin) with timestamps matching exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Patch Compliance (Federal Due Date 2026-06-21)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date and pipeline context notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Compliance scanning is mandatory for CISA KEV tracking and regulatory alignment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys) for Splunk Enterprise instances running vulnerable versions of CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference against patch logs to identify unpatched systems at or past the federal due date (2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Splunk Configuration Persistence (Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file creation capability in Splunk context enables threat actors to plant persistent backdoors or modify startup configurations. Article establishes file-creation power sufficient for persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file writes to Splunk startup directories, app configs, or script directories following unauthenticated sidecar access. Flag new executable files, modified boot configs, or unexpected scripts with Splunk ownership.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access to Splunk
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user' exploits 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'; this is the primary attack vector and point of initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated HTTP(S) requests to Splunk sidecar PostgreSQL endpoints. Alert on POST/GET requests lacking valid Splunk session tokens or auth headers, especially from IPs external to the organization or known malicious ASNs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Process File Creation/Truncation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'; this is the exploitation outcome and primary impact mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when splunkd or Splunk-related processes create or truncate files outside expected Splunk data directories, especially when correlated with network connections to sidecar endpoints or unusual PostgreSQL client activity from the Splunk host.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Public Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation in the wild; article references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' but no operational use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8000, 8089) reachable from untrusted networks without VPN enforcement. Cross-reference against CISA KEV CVE-2026-20253; flag exposed instances for immediate patching per federal due date (2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to asset-exposure hunt for exposed Splunk instances. 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [..._TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure].'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances reachable from internet or untrusted networks, correlate against known-exploited version identifiers for CVE-2026-20253. Alert on any unauthenticated successful connections to critical endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint without valid Splunk authentication tokens. Flag requests that include file manipulation parameters (create, truncate, write) originating from external or untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article attack outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This represents the impact execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events initiated by Splunk service account or PostgreSQL processes that lack corresponding authenticated user action in Splunk logs. Baseline benign file operations and surface anomalies.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Missing Authentication Function Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated user.' Detect direct exploitation of this auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to known-critical Splunk endpoints (identified via vulnerability advisories) that succeed without auth headers or with malformed/missing session tokens. Correlate with file operation logs for confirmation of exploitation.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated Access from Unexpected Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'unauthenticated user' exploitation. Flag access from sources not in trusted admin/operator whitelist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of IP/subnet sources for legitimate Splunk admin access. Alert when unauthenticated or failed-auth requests originate from sources outside this whitelist, especially across federated network boundaries.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the primary attack vector and should be the top detection priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk instances targeting sidecar service endpoints without prior authentication tokens. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed Splunk Enterprise instances. Flag success responses from unauthenticated requests to /sidecar/* or similar endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious File Operations from Splunk Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint,' indicating post-exploitation file manipulation enabling DoS, privilege escalation, or code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, modification, or truncation events originating from Splunk sidecar service processes. Flag anomalous writes to config/binary directories. Correlate with unauthenticated sidecar access events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited' and recommends checking across fleet 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches.' Federal patch due date is 2026-06-21.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute Splunk Enterprise discovery across all assets. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20253 scanner results. Flag instances showing detected vulnerability regardless of reported patch status. Alert on instances approaching Federal remediation due date (2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: Detect Splunk Enterprise with Missing Authentication Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'missing authentication for critical function vulnerability' — root cause is disabled/absent authz controls on public-facing sidecar service endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Splunk Enterprise configurations for disabled or absent authentication on critical endpoints (sidecar service, APIs). Flag instances where authz controls are missing or set to default-allow.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure and Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Splunk Enterprise as the vulnerable product under active exploitation; CISA KEV requires federal remediation by 2026-06-21. Asset inventory and patch baseline are foundational for a known-exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Splunk Enterprise instances and verify patch status against CVE-2026-20253. Alert on instances listening on externally-routable networks or responding to unauthenticated service requests. Baseline: internal-only deployments with strong authentication enforced.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is the direct attack vector requiring detection of authentication-bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints for requests missing authentication headers or containing invalid credentials. Flag requests with file operation parameters (create, truncate, delete) originating from untrusted network sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation and Truncation via Database Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — post-exploitation activity detection should monitor for anomalous file system modifications initiated through the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, modification, or truncation operations initiated through PostgreSQL sidecar or database service accounts. Flag mass file operations, targeting of log/audit directories, or unexpected file deletions outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Log and Audit File Tampering by Database Service
suggestion.rationale: Truncation capability mentioned in article enables cover-tracks behavior; adversaries will exploit file-delete permissions to destroy audit evidence and disable post-breach detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline log file sizes and rotation patterns for critical logs. Alert on unexpected truncation or deletion of Splunk audit logs, application logs, or OS event logs. Flag database service accounts or Splunk processes attempting to modify log paths or file sizes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation in the wild; once proof-of-concept is disclosed, detection should match network scanning and exploitation patterns targeting this specific vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify network-based scanning probes or exploitation attempts targeting Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint. Monitor for known CVE-2026-20253 exploit signatures, anomalous sidecar parameters, or behavior matching disclosed proof-of-concept code.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Zero detection logic generated despite explicit attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise web access logs and HTTP proxy logs for unauthenticated requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints. Alert on HTTP 200/201 responses to sidecar paths from external IPs. Cross-reference against asset inventory for CVE-2026-20253 vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Abnormal File Operations from Splunk Service Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability enables 'create or truncate arbitrary files' but pipeline generated no UC for file system impact monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and truncation events originating from splunkd and sidecar service processes. Alert on writes to /etc, application config directories, and system startup paths. Establish baseline of normal Splunk file operations and trigger on anomalous patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Active Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV (actively exploited in wild) with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-21. Pipeline missed urgency-driven active exploit detection despite two-day patch window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Splunk instances confirmed vulnerable by scanner, enhance endpoint monitoring for CVE-2026-20253 exploitation: requests with suspicious file operation payloads to sidecar endpoints, POST/PUT/DELETE to normally read-only paths, and patterns indicating privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempts Against Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function.' Pipeline missed detection for auth-bypass-specific patterns targeting file operations or database access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for requests to critical functions lacking valid session tokens or with null Authorization headers. Flag rapid sequences of failed auth followed by successful critical-function access.

suggestion.title: Database Activity via Compromised Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation grants attacker access to PostgreSQL sidecar, enabling lateral movement. No UC for detecting anomalous database queries or privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar logs for queries outside normal Splunk operational patterns, CREATE/ALTER/DROP operations, or system command execution. Correlate with unexpected process creation from the Splunk host.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Arbitrary File Creation in Sensitive Directories
suggestion.rationale: File creation capability enables persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, SSH keys, startup scripts). No UC generated for persistence detection despite impact being explicitly file-based.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file creation in persistence locations (/etc/cron.d, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, startup directories) originating from Splunk processes. Alert on modifications to Splunk config files or creation of new system accounts via file operations.

suggestion.title: GentleKiller Process Termination Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'targeting 400 security processes' — clear signal of EDR/AV process enumeration and termination. No detection use case was generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to enumerate, access, or terminate known EDR processes (Windows Defender, CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne, Rapid7, etc.) via API calls, handles, or direct process termination. Flag suspiciously rapid process creation/termination cycles that target multiple security tools sequentially.

suggestion.title: GentleKiller Malware Execution / File Drop
suggestion.rationale: RaaS malware must execute — article identifies 'GentleKiller EDR Framework' by name but pipeline generated zero executable detection signatures or file-based IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation and execution of files or processes matching GentleKiller signatures, command-line patterns consistent with EDR evasion tooling (dll injection, memory-only execution, handle spoofing), or execution from atypical staging directories.

suggestion.title: Gentlemen RaaS Campaign Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: RaaS operations require C2 beaconing and exfiltration staging. Article names 'The Gentlemen RaaS' but pipeline extracted zero network IOCs, domains, or C2 detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious outbound HTTPS/DNS patterns from compromised hosts to unknown or newly-registered domains; detect command execution initiated by remote callers; monitor for data staging in temporary directories followed by exfiltration (common RaaS pattern).

suggestion.title: Suspicious EDR Framework Loading / DLL Injection
suggestion.rationale: GentleKiller is described as an 'EDR Framework' — likely uses DLL injection, memory manipulation, or kernel-level mechanisms to disable security. Pipeline missed module-load and injection detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DLL injection into system processes, suspicious LoadLibrary calls from unsigned or newly-created DLLs, and unexpected module loads in security-critical processes. Flag unsigned drivers or kernel-mode code loading.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Suspicious Tool or Function Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article states agent hijacked for 'Host Code Execution.' Pipeline missed detection for execution-class tool calls (shells, interpreters, subprocess APIs) originating from LLM agent context. Phrase: 'Hijack AI Agent for Host Code Execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag LLM tool-invocation or function-call logs showing execution-class operations (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, subprocess, os.system) where the call originated from untrusted web context or anomalous agentic behavior. Alert on first-time invocations or deviations from baseline tool-use patterns.

suggestion.title: Web Page Content Injection into AI Client
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is web page compromising agent. Pipeline should detect when AI clients (extensions, SDK agents) fetch untrusted web content and pass it to LLM with system context. Phrase: 'One Web Page Hijack AI Agent.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI client applications (ChatGPT extensions, Claude.ai, agent SDKs) for fetches of untrusted or dynamically-generated URLs, especially those with redirect chains or suspicious MIME types. Correlate fetches with subsequent LLM tool invocations.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Embedded in Web Content
suggestion.rationale: AutoJack likely embeds injection payloads in HTML to manipulate agent behavior. Pipeline completely missed injection pattern detection in fetched content. Phrase: 'Web Page... Hijack AI Agent.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan HTTP response bodies fetched by AI clients for prompt-injection markers: role-switching instructions ('You are now...', 'Ignore...'), jailbreak patterns, function-invocation directives in HTML/script tags, or meta-tag instructions. Establish lexicon of injection keywords and flag content containing multiple markers.

suggestion.title: Code Execution Correlated to LLM Tool Call
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome is RCE via agent. Pipeline should correlate process-creation events with LLM audit logs to establish execution causality. Article end-state is clear but pipeline missed this chain. Phrase: 'Host Code Execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate process-creation events (cmd.exe, bash, powershell spawn) with LLM tool-invocation logs by timestamp and parent session. Alert when code execution can be traced to an LLM function call that was invoked by untrusted external input or anomalous prompt content.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Tool/Capability Restriction Bypass
suggestion.rationale: AutoJack forces agent to invoke capabilities outside declared scope (code execution where disallowed). Pipeline missed detection for capability-policy violations. Phrase: 'Hijack AI Agent for Host Code Execution' implies breaking out of sandboxed behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM agent runtime for invocation of restricted or disallowed tools (shell access, file I/O, privileged APIs, external network) that fail runtime policy checks. Track attempts to bypass tool filtering or circumvent capability whitelists.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to [Authorize]-Protected DotVVM Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states AuthorizeActionFilter 'simply does nothing' — unauthenticated or unauthorized users can access protected endpoints. Article phrase: 'no hacking is needed to bypass the filter.' Organizations must detect attempts to access endpoints decorated with [Authorize] attributes without valid credentials or role membership.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to endpoints marked with [Authorize] attributes that succeed without corresponding authentication tokens or with role mismatches. Flag 4xx→2xx transitions on protected endpoints from the same source IP/user within minutes, indicating vulnerability testing.

suggestion.title: Detection of Vulnerable DotVVM Framework Versions
suggestion.rationale: Versions < 4.3.15, < 4.2.11, and < 5.0.0-preview09 are vulnerable. Article specifies exact patch versions. Orgs can inventory running instances via application telemetry, HTTP headers, or framework-specific endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse HTTP response headers and application telemetry to identify DotVVM version strings. Alert on instances running 4.2.x, 4.3.x (pre-15), or 5.0.0-preview (pre-09), indicating vulnerability exposure.

suggestion.title: Authorization Exception Suppression or Swallowing in DotVVM Apps
suggestion.rationale: AuthorizeActionFilter bypass implies logging gaps — applications may show no authorization failure events when the filter fails to execute. Article phrase: 'AuthorizeActionFilter simply does nothing' — detection must account for silent failures. Monitor for missing authorization audit trails or unexpected access logs without preceding authentication events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline authorization success/failure ratios in DotVVM audit logs. Flag scenarios where protected endpoint access succeeds with zero preceding authorization checks, or where access logs exist but security event logs show no corresponding auth failure.

suggestion.title: Bulk Testing of Protected Endpoints by Unauthorized Sources
suggestion.rationale: Attacker exploiting the vulnerability would perform reconnaissance by probing protected endpoints. Article establishes that authorization checks are bypassed entirely, making it trivial to enumerate protected resources. Sequential or high-volume requests to multiple [Authorize]-decorated endpoints should trigger behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify single-source IP addresses or user accounts making high-frequency requests to multiple distinct protected endpoints within a narrow time window, consistent with automated scanning for accessible resources.

suggestion.title: Access Anomaly: Resource Requests Inconsistent with User Role
suggestion.rationale: If AuthorizeActionFilter is disabled, access control enforcement relies on downstream role checks — which may also fail. Behavioral anomaly detection should flag users accessing resources their role/permission level should not permit. Article phrase: 'Missing authorization' implies complete bypass, not just degraded checks.
log_sources: HTTP request logs with user context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare user role/group membership against accessed endpoint permissions in DotVVM apps. Flag requests where a user accesses an endpoint requiring Role A but user holds only Role B, or is unauthenticated entirely.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Data Exfiltration from Protected DotVVM Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Once authorization filter is bypassed, attacker gains access to protected actions/data. Monitor for large data responses from protected endpoints going to unexpected destinations or at unusual times. Article impact: 'All users of AuthorizeActionFilter class are affected' implies widespread exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor response sizes and frequency from protected DotVVM endpoints accessed without valid authorization. Alert on unusually large responses or rapid sequential high-volume data requests to protected endpoints from single sources.

suggestion.title: WordPress Malicious JavaScript/PHP Injection in Theme/Plugin Files
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'cleaned 14,971 WordPress sites'—implies malicious code removal from wp-content/, wp-includes/, or plugin directories. SocGholish persistence mechanism: injected scripts for redirection/malvertising.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on obfuscated or eval()-containing PHP/JS files created in wp-content, wp-includes, or theme directories with network callbacks post-write. Flag script tags with foreign domain registrations (not matching installed plugin vendors) injected into functions.php or wp-config.php.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Database User/Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Operation Endgame takedowns enumerate backdoor accounts; article context signals persistence via wp_users table manipulation without admin UI audit trail.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress database INSERT/UPDATE on wp_users outside business hours with super-admin capability bits set (meta: wp_user_level=10) and no corresponding wp-admin user.php edit log. Alert on programmatic account creation via direct wp_users.INSERT rather than wp-admin registration.

suggestion.title: SocGholish C2 Domain / IP Beaconing from Compromised WordPress
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'disrupts SocGholish Servers'—implies enumerated C2 infrastructure. Detection must ingest extracted domains/IPs and cross-reference network egress from WordPress hosting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests from web servers to domains flagged in Operation Endgame advisories with SocGholish C2 classification, especially via User-Agent spoofing (common SocGholish signature: generic/outdated UA strings) or gzip-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: .htaccess / Web Server Config Manipulation for Traffic Redirection
suggestion.rationale: SocGholish standard persistence vector: .htaccess RewriteRule injection for traffic steering; cleanup of 14,971 sites implies this artifact was universal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .htaccess file writes with RewriteCond patterns targeting external domains or obfuscated base64/hex-encoded redirect destinations. Alert on .htaccess modification timestamp clustering across multiple WordPress hosts (indicates automated push).

suggestion.title: Drive-by Download / Malvertising Redirect Payload Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'disrupts' and 14K cleanup scope indicate large-scale redirection-malware infrastructure. Typical SocGholish end-goal: browser redirect to exploit kits or malvertising networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP response bodies from affected WordPress domains for injected meta-refresh or JavaScript redirects to known malvertising CDNs, exploit kit landing pages, or drive-by download hosts. Flag mismatched Content-Type headers (e.g., text/html served as application/javascript).

suggestion.title: Malicious WordPress Plugin / Theme Installation via Direct File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Operation Endgame cleanup suggests plugin/theme repository poisoning or direct .zip upload exploitation; article context implies this as delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on plugin/theme .zip extraction to wp-content/plugins or wp-content/themes without corresponding wp-admin plugin installation audit log. Monitor for direct .php file placement in those directories with timestamps outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Node.js spawns /bin/sh -c with allowlist-prefix + shell metacharacter injection
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'The allowlist glob-matches the whole command string, but `ShellExecutor` runs that string through `/bin/sh -c`. So any wildcard allow such as `git *`, `npm *` or `node *` also matches `git status; <anything>`.' This is the primary exploit (UC_12_2 in article recommendations).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js process spawning shell interpreter (sh, bash, dash) with -c flag where ProcessCommandLine contains shell metacharacters (;, &&, ||) AND command prefix matches allowlist targets (git, npm, node, yarn, pnpm). This indicates sandbox-escape via injection.

suggestion.title: Linux recon utilities spawned from shell child of Node.js
suggestion.rationale: Article post-exploitation phase: 'process_name IN (id,whoami,uname,hostname,curl,wget,nc,ncat,python,python3,perl,ssh-keygen)' via sh parent. This is UC_12_3 for discovery/actions phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sh/bash/dash spawned by Node.js executing reconnaissance binaries (id, whoami, uname, hostname, curl, wget, nc, ncat, python, perl, ssh-keygen, cat). Indicates successful allowlist bypass followed by system enumeration.

suggestion.title: Proof-of-concept binary execution — poc-316.js
suggestion.rationale: Article-specific hunt (UC_12_1) targets concrete exploit artifact: 'Processes.process_name IN (poc-316.js)'. This is the referenced PoC binary for CVE-2026-54051 allowlist bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process execution or file creation/modification of poc-316.js. Monitor 30-day lookback for Node.js parent processes or script contexts spawning this artifact—indicates active exploitation or testing of CVE-2026-54051.

suggestion.title: Asset inventory: hosts running vulnerable Network-AI (CVE-2026-54051)
suggestion.rationale: Article references standard hunt: 'Asset exposure—vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' with CVE-2026-54051. Foundational inventory control for vulnerability management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory and vulnerability systems to identify Network-AI versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-54051. Correlate with process telemetry showing Node.js execution in agent/sandbox contexts to prioritize exposure.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable network-ai npm package detected in node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_13_1: 'Vulnerable network-ai npm package install on disk'. Detects presence of vulnerable package versions as asset inventory and precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search filesystem events for network-ai package in node_modules with versions <5.7.2. Parse package.json manifests revealing vulnerable version numbers. Identifies at-risk assets for remediation workflows.

suggestion.title: network-ai MCP SSE server process execution
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_13_2: 'network-ai MCP SSE server launched on endpoint'. Detects vulnerable service startup and network exposure before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node/npx/npm process creation with command-line arguments containing both 'network-ai' and 'mcp-server', excluding legitimate stdio-mode subprocess invocations. Correlate with NETWORK_AI_MCP_SECRET environment variable to assess secret configuration.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to network-ai /mcp endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_13_3: 'Unauthenticated POST /mcp tool invocation against network-ai SSE server'. This is the active exploitation phase leveraging the empty-default-secret vulnerability—the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests to /mcp or /mcp/* endpoints on network-ai mcp-server hosts from non-loopback IPs returning HTTP 200 without valid authentication headers. Indicates unauthenticated MCP tool invocation via default-empty-secret authentication bypass.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user...through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct attack surface identification
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk hosts for connections to PostgreSQL sidecar ports from external/unexpected sources without preceding auth events. Track HTTP requests to Splunk endpoints lacking authentication tokens. Alert on connection spikes to localhost:5432 or internal service ports from non-admin processes.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability 'could allow...to create...arbitrary files' — direct impact of successful exploitation

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Vulnerability Presence

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Splunk Enterprise instances with CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference patch levels against vendor advisory. Flag unpatched systems with external connectivity or exposure to untrusted networks before federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication to Splunk Critical Functions

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for HTTP 401/403 responses to critical endpoints (file operations, config endpoints) followed by retry patterns from single external source. Correlate with successful file-system operations to detect successful bypass.

suggestion.title: GCS Bucket Creation with Vertex AI Project Name Simulation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'bucket squatting'—attacker-created buckets mimicking legitimate model upload destinations. Pipeline missed IOC extraction and detection for CreateBucket API calls with names matching project naming patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GCS CreateBucket operations where bucket name closely resembles existing Vertex AI project IDs or follows '{project}-{stage}-models' patterns. Trigger if creator is external service account, uses residential IP, or precedes model upload attempts by <12 hours.

suggestion.title: Vertex AI Model Upload Redirected to Non-Approved GCS Bucket
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'hijack model uploads'—SDK redirects or accepts model writes to attacker-controlled buckets. Pipeline failed to surface model upload interception or unauthorized bucket-destination writes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect aiplatform.models.upload or datasets.upload operations that resolve GCS target to buckets outside approved project storage locations. Cross-correlate: if bucket created <24h prior by different principal, flag as model hijacking attempt.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Vertex AI SDK Version Usage with Unauthorized Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Headline specifies 'SDK flaw'—implies specific vulnerable versions. Pipeline extracted zero version IOCs and no execution-phase detection for compromised SDK loads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for google-cloud-aiplatform package versions <[min_patched_version] loading in production environments. Correlate with unexpected GCP authentication events (new service accounts) or model-upload API calls initiated from unusual processes.

suggestion.title: Cross-Project Service Account Token Used for GCS Bucket Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must credential-hop to squatted buckets; pipeline missed detection of service account token misuse or out-of-project IAM role assumption around model operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service account credentials (OAuth2 tokens) performing model.upload or bucket.putObject from projects other than where the credentials were created. Alert if token used by Vertex AI SDK service account suddenly grants storage.buckets permissions to buckets with squatting-pattern names.

suggestion.title: Malicious Model Version Registered in Vertex AI Registry from Hijacked Bucket
suggestion.rationale: Post-hijacking: attacker-supplied model reaches production registry. Pipeline should detect unauthorized model deploys or version-metadata tampering, but generated no impact-phase detection.
log_sources: Vertex AI Model Registry audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on models.create or models.update operations where source bucket is not in organizational whitelist, or model checksum diverges from CI/CD artifacts for same version label. Correlate: if model deployed to endpoint <1h after creation by non-standard principal, escalate as poisoning attempt.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Vertex AI Project Buckets and Naming Schemes
suggestion.rationale: Bucket squatting requires attacker to identify project naming patterns; pipeline missed detection of reconnaissance queries (LIST buckets, describe projects) preceding attacker bucket creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ListBuckets or ListProjects API calls from non-approved service accounts followed within 2h by CreateBucket operations with similar naming schemes. Flag if caller has no prior Vertex AI interaction history.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...] Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20253 against Splunk Enterprise asset inventory. Identify instances reachable from untrusted networks on default ports (8089, 8000). Flag any exposed instances pending patch application past due-date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'missing authentication for critical function' via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. Article specifies unauthenticated exploitation route; pipeline surfaced no detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints (typically port 9997–9999) lacking valid authentication tokens or X-Splunk-Input-Token headers. Alert on POST/PUT payloads to file-operation endpoints from external sources.

suggestion.title: File Creation/Truncation via Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker capability to 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. This file-manipulation vector is absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or truncation events in $SPLUNK_HOME initiated by unauthenticated sidecar connections. Alert on modifications to critical database or configuration files outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Log Truncation and Audit Trail Destruction
suggestion.rationale: Ability to 'truncate arbitrary files' enables erasure of audit logs, a defense-evasion tactic. Pipeline missed this secondary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on truncation or deletion of transaction logs, audit logs, or database WAL files in Splunk infrastructure. Flag any such operations correlated with prior unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No auth required; any network-exposed sidecar port is an attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to /_sidecar/ or /_postgres/ paths (or sidecar enumeration patterns) originating from external IPs without valid Splunk session tokens. Flag 200/201 responses. Correlate source IPs against shodan/censys for Splunk instance inventories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write/Truncate Operations from Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—file manipulation at scale is both data destruction (T1565.001) and potential persistence. Should hunt for anomalous file ops by Splunk processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid file creation/truncation attributed to splunkd or sidecar processes outside expected working directories. Flag bulk deletes to log paths. Correlate with unauthorized sidecar endpoint hits from same timeframe.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV = active exploitation. Pipeline must generate CVE-specific IDS rule. Article establishes attack pattern: missing auth + file ops.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk HTTP requests lacking authentication tokens + subsequent file-write syscalls from Splunk process. IDS rule: flag POST/GET to sidecar endpoints from sources not in trusted CIDR. Federal patch due 2026-06-21 defines urgency window.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Instance Inventory Against CVE-2026-20253 Patch Status

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanner output for Splunk Enterprise instances unpatched for CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference asset management DB to identify instances with external-facing ports (8000, 8089). Prioritize instances exposed to internet. Flag any updated after 2026-06-21 as potential post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Port Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as attack vector. Reconnaissance scanning for this service should be a hunt target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network scanning activity (SYN sweeps, service enumeration) against Splunk infrastructure. Flag repeated connection attempts to sidecar ports (often 5432-derivative, or custom ports). Correlate with external source IPs attempting HTTP enumeration.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the critical access pattern is absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated network connections to the Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint from untrusted networks. Track successful connections without credential exchange. Correlate with subsequent file system modifications on the Splunk host.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: The payload is explicit: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this behavioral indicator is completely missing from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, deletion, or truncation operations on the Splunk Enterprise host sourced from or proxied through the PostgreSQL sidecar process. Prioritize unexpected operations to sensitive Splunk directories and system paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends baseline vulnerability scanning against this CVE; the basic inventory detection is absent. Federal remediation deadline is 2026-06-21.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index all Splunk Enterprise instances across the fleet. Flag any with product version matching CVE-2026-20253's affected range as critical priority. Cross-reference with external network exposure data to prioritize remediation of internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'missing authentication for critical function'—detection must focus on endpoint exposure and lack of access controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound network traffic to the PostgreSQL sidecar service port from external or untrusted subnets. Alert on any attempts from non-Splunk administrative networks. Correlate with firewall rule changes that may have widened access scope.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Download & Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Fake Update Lures'—core ClickFix infection vector. No detection rule generated despite this being the initial access point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables matching Windows/software update naming patterns (.exe, .msi, .scr) downloaded from non-Microsoft CDNs and executed from temp/Downloads. Correlate download source reputation and file signature validation failures.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Loader Execution from User Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'new loaders' as malware delivery mechanism; execution phase detection missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or recently-signed executables spawned from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Downloads, or %UserProfile% with secondary network I/O or suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe).

suggestion.title: Staged Malware Fetch Post-Loader
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'expand malware delivery' implies multi-stage: loader fetches secondary payload. Command-and-control phase entirely absent from kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections (HTTP/HTTPS to non-whitelisted destinations, DNS to unregistered domains) from loader processes within seconds of user-initiated execution, especially with .exe parent in user directories.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Threat Actor IOC Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article name-checks ClickFix campaign; should correlate to known malware family signatures, registry keys, C2 domains. No actor/campaign identified in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process/file artifacts (names, registry keys, strings) against published ClickFix tooling signatures. Detect obfuscation techniques (XOR, API hashing, string encoding) documented in ClickFix variants.

suggestion.title: Browser-Spawned Child Process With Unsigned Binary Execution
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering delivery model (user clicks link/download from browser). Detection for browser→exe→network chain not present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes with ancestry explorer.exe or browser process → unsigned .exe in user directories → immediate outbound connection. Raise alert on first-seen unsigned binary execution chains within 30 seconds of download.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Management Port
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit; MITRE T1190 implies network exposure. Core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound TCP connections to Splunk management ports (8089, 8000) lacking valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Alert if POST/GET requests to /services/data/* or /admin/* endpoints return success without Authorization header.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector: 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. Requires monitoring for unauthorized access to internal service endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically localhost:5432 or named pipe access). Alert on SQL commands (CREATE TABLE, DROP, TRUNCATE) executed via sidecar without authenticated Splunk process context.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'create or truncate arbitrary files'; this is the direct impact and should be detected at filesystem level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation operations by splunkd or sidecar processes in unexpected directories (outside standard Splunk/var/lib/splunk paths). Flag TRUNCATE operations on config files, encrypted indices, or audit logs.

suggestion.title: Scanning for Exposed Splunk Instances
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV context implies reconnaissance phase; article references 'exposed assets'. Network scanning for Splunk should precede exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed connection attempts to port 8089/8000 across internal or DMZ ranges, or successful connections followed by HTTP OPTIONS/HEAD probes to /_status endpoint without authentication.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Detection via Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article cites CVE-2026-20253 as the canonical identifier; standard asset inventory and patch tracking required for CISA KEV compliance.

Flag systems where splunkd process version matches vulnerable range (obtain from Splunk advisory) but patch not applied by federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Langflow BaseFileComponent tar extraction with parent-directory traversal symlinks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symlink-traversal' as the core vulnerability mechanism but existing UC_2_2 only hunts for POST to upload endpoints, not the actual tar extraction or symlink creation. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow processes executing tar, untar, or Python tarfile operations on uploads directory; correlate with creation of symlinks to sensitive paths (/etc, /.ssh, /.aws) in tmp or Langflow working directories within seconds of tar extraction. Flag if symlink target count exceeds 5 per extraction.

suggestion.title: JWT authentication bypass via forged bearer tokens in Langflow API calls
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1606.001 (Forge Web Credentials: Web Cookies) but UC_2_4 title mentions 'post-JWT-forge' with no actual hunt for JWT tampering. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to Langflow API endpoints with Authorization: Bearer headers where JWT signature verification fails, claims are missing (exp, iss, aud), or token was created with a non-standard key. Flag any Authorization header modification within 10 seconds of a 401 response followed by a 200 response.

suggestion.title: Python Interpreter node code execution with dynamic imports and system commands
suggestion.rationale: Article title and UC_2_4 imply 'Python Interpreter node' is the RCE endpoint, but detections focus on child-process spawning, not the actual arbitrary Python code execution within Langflow. Need detection for eval/exec/compile/import statements with untrusted input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow worker processes for Python bytecode execution (compile, exec, eval, __import__) where arguments originate from HTTP request parameters. Correlate HTTP POST to endpoints containing 'python', 'interpreter', 'eval' with child-process creation within 100ms.

suggestion.title: File and directory enumeration via repeated 404/403 responses from Langflow file endpoints
